Feeling fit? Hike up Barr Trail to the summit, especially beautiful in the summer with all the wild flowers. Feeling really fit? Run up during the Pikes Peak Ascent or run up ''and'' down in the Pikes Peak Marathon.

see.name: Rock Ledge Ranch
see.desc: A seasonal living history museum ranging across four time periods encompassing authentic American Indian, early settler, Victorian and Edwardian eras.

see.name: Cave of the Winds
see.desc: A series of caves near Manitou Springs, offering tours.

see.name: Cheyenne Mountain Zoo
see.desc: A small, scenic mountain zoo with many exotic animals.

see.name: Seven Falls
see.desc: A privately owned series of falls and nature trails. Fills up quickly on weekends, but you can instead visit neighboring Helen Hunt Falls.

see.name: Helen Hunt Falls
see.desc: A short hike to some great views, within '''[http://www.springsgov.com/Page.asp?NavID=3038 North Cheyenne Cañon City Park]'''.

see.name: United States Olympic Training Center
see.desc: Major U.S. Olympic training facility, with an aquatic center, gymnasiums, shooting center, and velodrome. Senior, group and military discounts are available.

see.name: United States Air Force Academy
see.desc: The main officer cadet school for the United States Air Force and Space Force. Founded in 1954, it does not have the same classical-style buildings of some of the other academies, but the campus is nestled in the foothills of the Rampart range with breathtaking scenery, and the Cadet Chapel is widely regarded an icon of modernist architecture. Tours are available year round during regular visiting hours.

see.name: Air Force Falcons
see.desc: The Academy's athletic program offers college sports action throughout the school year. The best-known program is the football team, long a solidly competitive program. Football games especially offer a unique combination of military pageantry and traditional college sports atmosphere. Ticket prices vary by sport.

see.name: Colorado College Tigers
see.desc: The Tigers play most of their sports in the non-scholarship NCAA Division III. However, two sports—men's ice hockey and women's soccer—play in Division I. The hockey team, which plays at Ed Robson Arena on its campus as a member of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference, has one of the richest traditions in U.S. college hockey. Its rivalry with the University of Denver is one of the fiercest in the sport.

see.name: May Natural History Museum
see.desc: An eclectic but unique museum south of town, with thousands of large insects collected by John May from around the tropics.

see.name: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and Museum of the American Cowboy
see.desc: The only heritage center in the world devoted to professional rodeo, with two multi-media presentations and Hall of Champions.

see.name: Garden of the Gods Trading Post
see.desc: Don't miss the largest art gallery and gift shop in Colorado. Sample delicious buffalo burgers and more at the Balanced Rock Cafe, on the outdoor patio, under the shade of the cottonwood trees.

see.name: Ghost Town Museum
see.desc: Step back in time to Colorado's gold-rush days and experience an 1800s old west town frozen in time. Pan for real gold!

see.name: Western Museum of Mining and Industry
see.desc: Featuring hands-on exhibits, gold panning, a working steam engine and Oro and Nugget, mascot burros!

see.name: Rocky Mountain Vibes
see.desc: The local Pioneer League (low minor league) baseball team plays at {{marker

see.name: Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC
see.desc: The local soccer team plays in the second-level USL Championship at {{marker

see.name: Penny Arcade Manitou Springs
see.desc: A historic location in Manitou Springs just outside of Colorado Springs where you can play old and new arcade games.

see.name: Academy Riding Stables
see.desc: Enjoy a ride through beautiful towering sandstone rock formations in the Garden of the Gods.

see.name: Challenge Unlimited-Pikes Peak by Bike
see.desc: Bike down over 7,000 feet from the top of Pikes Peak with professional guides, mid-April–October. Bike helmet, all-weather gear and meals are included.

see.name: The Colorado Climbing Company
see.desc: Climb with certified, professional guides in the Garden of the Gods, Cheyenne Cañon, Red Rock Canyon, and more.

see.name: IVP at the Beach House Volleyball
see.desc: Sand

see.name: ACBL Unit 360 Bridge Center
see.desc: Sanctioned duplicate games most afternoons and many evenings (except Sunday).

see.name: Pikes Peak Center for the Performing Arts

eat.name: Il Vicino Wood Oven Pizza & Brewery
eat.desc: Great gourmet pizzas.

eat.name: Shuga's
eat.desc: Funky.

eat.name: Biaggis
eat.desc: Great gourmet Italian food.

eat.name: Jake and Telly's
eat.desc: Great Greek food; under $15 for lunch, over $20 for dinner. Sit outside on their second floor patio and enjoy the gorgeous Colorado Springs weather.

eat.name: O'Furry's
eat.desc: Hole-in-the-wall Irish-style pub, featuring some of the best burgers in Colorado Springs.

eat.name: Frankie's Bar & Grill
eat.desc: Neighborhood bar/grill since 1984.Burgers and wings. Perfect for watching all the games.

eat.name: Jun Japanese
eat.desc: Very good Japanese - Popular happy hour

eat.name: Rico's Coffee and Wine Bar
eat.desc: Wine, chocolate, coffee, tapas, and great music.

eat.name: Pueblo Viejo
eat.desc: Authentic Mexican food. Run by a family from [[Jalisco]], Mexico who specialize in chile rellenos. Great salsa and atmosphere.

eat.name: The Airplane Restaurant
eat.desc: Ok diner, and you can eat inside a KC-97 aircraft, lots of aviation decor.

eat.name: Sheldon's Luncheonette
eat.desc: Awesome breakfast and daily meat sandwiches or plates for lunch.

eat.name: O'sae Sushi Ramen Bistro
eat.desc: O’sae offers authentic and delicious tasting Japanese cuisine and bistro in Colorado Springs, CO. O’sae's convenient location makes this restaurant a natural choice for dine-in or take-out meals in the Colorado Spring community. The restaurant is known for its variety in taste and choice of meals. Customers can state their personal taste preferences upon arrival and then take delight in the individualized maki, sushi, salad, and ramen creations. A true new way to do your traditional O’sae style meal.

eat.name: Slice420
eat.desc: Great New York style pizza. Founded by a family of American medical refugees who actively support/donate to American medical refugee causes, HopeKids, The Shandy Clinic, Mt. Carmel Veterans Service Center, Flowering Hope Foundation, and local businesses and individuals in need. Offers pizza by the slice, full pizza pies, calzones, pizza rolls, salads, desserts, etc.

eat.name: Bristol Brewing Company
eat.desc: In an old elementary school. Quite charming and unique.

eat.name: Phantom Canyon Brewing Co.
eat.desc: Wide variety of excellent brews made on premises. Also serves high quality food for lunch and dinner daily. Brunch is available Sunday only.

eat.name: Jack Quinns Irish Pub
eat.desc: Great Irish and English beers, decent Irish food. Stay for the Irish band!

eat.name: Trinity Brewing Co
eat.desc: Great micro brewery! Has 4-6 of their own beers on tap as well as an ever changing selection of 28 Plus other micro beers. Great food. Great crowd. Free Wi-Fi.

see.name: University of Colorado Boulder
see.desc: The flagship institution of the state of Colorado, CU (as it's called locally) has a 600-acre campus, with beautiful gardens and buildings tucked away in its mainly pedestrian core that's worth a visit. Check out the [http://cuheritage.org/ Heritage Center] located in the Old Main building, for a look at the history of CU. There are also art galleries and museums throughout campus.

see.name: Colorado Buffaloes
see.desc: CU's sports teams are among the city's best-known attractions, competing in seven men's and 10 women's sports, mostly in the Big 12 Conference. The biggest draw is the football team, which has had a rich tradition (as well as the larger-than-life personality of current head coach Deion Sanders), though it's struggled to regain its prominence. Men's basketball, and to a lesser extent women's basketball, are also significant draws. Football plays at {{marker

see.name: Boulder Creek Path
see.desc: This miles-long path sits on the banks of the Boulder Creek, cutting right through the middle of town. Along this path you will find beautiful walking, biking, and other forms of recreation. In the downtown area, pick up the path at Civic Park on Broadway, between Canyon and Arapaho Avenues. In the summer, many parts of the creek become popular swimming holes. You can buy (and fill) inner tubes at local gas stations, should you want to have a down-the-creek journey. It follows Boulder Creek, making this path anything but boring.

see.name: Chautauqua Park
see.desc: At the base of the Flatiron's rock formations. For a minor hike, take the trail to the 3rd Flatiron. This hike will show you sweeping vistas of town and an up-close and personal look at the Flatiron's rock formations. During the summer months, the Boulder Symphony performs at Chautauqua, with the mountains as a stunning backdrop. The '''Chautauqua Auditorium''' is a large wooden building constructed in 1898, and there is a restaurant (the Dining Hall) which was built at the same time.

see.name: Whitewater Tube Co.
see.desc: During summer time, it is popular to go tubing on Boulder Creek. Either rent from Whitewater or buy a tube at a local service station (the service station at NE corner of Arapahoe Avenue and Broadway is very popular for tube purchase. It also has a free air hose if your own tube needs inflating).

see.name: Happy Thursday Cruising
see.desc: Every Thursday during the summer, a lot of people gather up in front of wahoo's restaurant and go around the city with bikes. Each week they have a different theme to wear.

see.name: NCAR Trails
see.desc: Green Mountain, Bear Mountain Trails.

see.name: Celestial Seasonings Tea Factory
see.desc: Take the tour through this famous tea company. Check out the mint room, it is ''very'' intense.

see.name: Fox Theatre
see.desc: A great music venue on the hill. Has been nominated for best venue in the US.

see.name: Flagstaff Mountain
see.desc: Flagstaff Mountain is a must-do. Follow Baseline Road West up the mountain, it is a windy, long road but the view is breathtaking. From up top, there is a beautiful view looking down on Boulder. The view from the other side is the Rocky Mountains. There are picnic areas, an amphitheater, bike and walking trails, Summit Nature Center, the Flagstaff House and views that you can not get anywhere else. A great place to relax or enjoy with friends.

see.name: South Boulder Creek Trail
see.desc: Good walking and biking trail, but the unique feature of this trail is that there are prairie dogs everywhere!

see.name: Eldorado Canyon State Park
see.desc: Eldorado Canyon State Park is a local state park to see the wilderness and beauty of this Colorado area.

see.name: Eldora Mountain Resort
see.desc: 21 miles west of Boulder. This easy to get to mountain (via car or RTD) is a local ski resort if travelers do not want to make the 2 hours trip to the main Colorado mountains.

see.name: Boulder Convention & Visitors Bureau
see.desc: Offering visitor information for your next visit to the area, including maps, hotel information, dining guides, meeting information and more. Visit one of our two visitor kiosks for brochures and maps, Davidson Mesa Overlook, several miles southeast of Boulder on US 36 or Pearl Street Mall, in front of the Courthouse between 13th and 14th streets.

eat.name: Efrain's II
eat.desc: This restaurant is a small dive that serves up excellent, authentic Mexican food. A little out of the way on the east side of town, it is well worth the drive.

eat.name: China Gourmet
eat.desc: Just north of town, China Gourmet is a local restaurant that has been serving up great Chinese food at reasonable prices for years.

eat.name: Khow Thai
eat.desc: Tucked into a small space on the east side of Broadway just south of Arapahoe Ave, this restaurant has repeatedly been voted the best Thai food in Boulder. Not expensive and really good, especially the green curry. The owner is surprisingly anti-vegan, so don't expect gracious substitutions or a warm reception.

eat.name: The Kitchen
eat.desc: A fantastic neighborhood bistro that sources most of its food from local growers and producers. Open 7 days a week for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Check out Monday night's Community Dinner, a $35 prix fixe meal that's off-menu, served family style around a huge table -- it's the best deal in town for the variety, quality, and quantity of food (reservations recommended).

eat.name: Kim's Vietnamese Food to Go
eat.desc: A fantastic Asian hole-in-the-wall. It's a little shack facing broadway in a parking lot. Kim makes everything fresh in front of your eyes and the place is very homey and fits in well with Boulder lifestyle. A hit among college students, it's a great place.

eat.name: Boulder Dushanbe Teahouse
eat.desc: A great place to enjoy a cup of tea and enjoy architecture from half way around the world. The food is moderately portioned and deliciously prepared. In the summers, outside dining is available, and when the rose garden is in bloom it is amazing.

eat.name: Illegal Pete's
eat.desc: A favorite for students of CU-Boulder, there is a location on the Hill, close to Jones Drugs, across the street from the CU Economics Building, and one on the far east side of the Pearl Street Mall. Economically priced, very generously proportioned Mexican food and beer. Perfect college town restaurant. The burritos are out of this world.

eat.name: West End Tavern
eat.desc: The classic American tavern is reborn! The rooftop deck is open (weather permitting), affording remarkable views of the Flatirons beneath 300 days of sunshine a year. Visit the Boulder locals' favorite for a cold brew and some good eats.

eat.name: Brasserie Ten Ten
eat.desc: For a more expensive meal, visit Brasserie 1010, on Walnut Street downtown, where French-inspired cuisine is served in an elegant setting with delicious daily specials.

eat.name: Sushi Zanmai
eat.desc: Zanmai is a traditional sushi house with the best rolls in town. Reasonably priced, watch as sushi chefs prepare your meal at the sushi bar. For the best deals, go to Happy Hour, from 5PM-6:30PM or all day Sunday. Try the Z-Number 9 and the Firecracker role or for an appetizer try the green mussels.

eat.name: Flagstaff House
eat.desc: Tucked up on Flagstaff Mountain, the Flagstaff House has breathtaking views of the City of Boulder just below it. Visit for cocktails, dessert, or stay for a full meal, the views will astonish you. Located up Baseline Ave, on Flagstaff Mountain, just 3 minutes outside of town. The checks are as steep as the Flat Irons, but if you are just visiting Boulder, this is a definite must!

eat.name: Mountain Sun/Southern Sun
eat.desc: On the east end of the Pearl Street walking mall, the Mountain Sun is well known for homebrewed beers, but also serves seriously tasty American fare. In the last 5 years, it built a sister restaurant in South Boulder, the Southern Sun, that is roomier and even more raucous. It's loud and filled with earthy Boulder locals. At dinner no matter what day of the week, you may wait for 20–30 minutes for a booth, but their quesadillas, nachos, salads, burgers, pizzas, and vegetarian options are sure to please every time. (Note: Neither the Mountain or Southern Sun accept credit cards, and can be flaky about out-of-state checks. Both have ATMs onsite.)

eat.name: Boulder Cork
eat.desc: A high quality restaurant since 1969, serving excellent dishes from prime rib to lobster ravioli. On the west side of 30th street.

eat.name: Sherpa's
eat.desc: Run by Pemba Sherpa, this restaurant is just outside off Broadway and Pearl. Featuring authentic Nepalese food that is made fresh to order, this restaurant is a must of Boulder.

eat.name: Jax Fish House & Oyster Bar
eat.desc: Home to ''Top Chef'' Season 5 winner Hosea Rosenberg.

eat.name: Red Rock Coffeehouse
eat.desc: In the Safeway shopping center on the corner of 28th and Iris. Locally-owned cafe serving locally roasted Organic Fair Trade Coffee, local food and pastries, naturally brewed Sanctuary Chai and locally Micro-Blended Tea.

eat.name: Rincon Argentino
eat.desc: Traditional Argentinian empanadas carefully crafted with local, natural ingredients and delectable recipes and served in an adorable ambiance soaked with Argentinian culture. Sip on a traditional mate while watching a soccer game, or sit on their beautiful patio and admire Boulder's iconic foothills. A local legend!

eat.name: The Sink
eat.desc: The sink is a Boulder institution with its colorful walls, great food and stories past (Robert Redford was the janitor) it attracts a large crowd for burgers, beer, gourmet pizza, and drinks almost every day of the week. Bring a black magic marker, and you can sign your name on the ceiling like generations of graduating CU seniors. Do not write on the walls, though.

eat.name: Mountain Sun/Southern Sun
eat.desc: Two locations in Boulder. The original Mountain Sun is on the east end of Pearl Street while newer location, called the Southern Sun, is in South Boulder at the intersection of South Broadway and Table Mesa in the Table Mesa Shopping Center. Some excellent beers (particularly the Java Porter) and often excellent Boulder granola music. Remember that it's a cash only bar.

eat.name: Boulder Beer
eat.desc: Claims to be Colorado's first microbrewery, but there is no doubt that their beers have been around forever in Boulder. Brewery/Pub is in north Boulder (in what always seemed an odd location) near the train tracks and off of Valmont near Foothills Parkway. They make great beers and have excellent happy hour deals.

eat.name: Walnut Brewery
eat.desc: Many classic beers that Boulderites rave about years after they leave Boulder. Located in the heart of Boulder on Walnut St, near 11th. Parking can be a pain in this area; best to use the parking garage across the street and hope for validation of your ticket.

eat.name: Frasca's Food and Wine
eat.desc: World-class Northern Italian cuisine. The tasting menu can be pricey, but the food is astounding.

eat.name: Dark Horse Bar and Grill
eat.desc: A total dive pub with beer, burgers, and bands. The walls are plastered with memorabilia and whirling machinery. The ceiling is lined with suspended hearses.

eat.name: Sanitas Brewing Co.
eat.desc: A brewery with a small tap room on site.

see.name: Skiing
see.desc: The ski resort has a good mix of beginner, intermediate as well as some of the steepest advanced ski you can want. And it's never crowded!

see.name: Telluride Outside
see.desc: Adventure guide service since 1984. Fly Fishing, 4WD tours, whitewater rafting and mountain bike tours.

eat.name: La Cocina de Luz
eat.desc: Mexican food bar.

eat.name: Baked in Telluride
eat.desc: Bakery, sandwiches and pizzas.

eat.name: Cindybread
eat.desc: A premier sandwich experience that tops some New York delis.

see.name: John Denver Park
see.desc: This Aspen park is a pleasant place to take your dog or your kids for a splash in the creek in summertime. The park is named after the famous Country and Folk singer who resided in Aspen. Lyrics from his most popular songs are inscribed in the creekside boulders. John Denver Park is on the creek trail on the north side of Aspen, near the Rio Grande Ball Field and park at N. Mill St. and Rio Grande Pl.

see.name: Maroon Bells
see.desc: A short drive outside of Aspen, the Maroon Bells are one of the most photographed mountain scenes in Colorado. The lake and views of the 14,000 foot peaks are spectacular. In the summer months between 8AM and 5PM, visitors must take a shuttle bus to the Maroon Bells to control traffic. Tickets are $6 for adults and $4 for children. There are some short, non-strenuous hikes around the Maroon Bells that vary from 1 mile to 10. People also like to climb the Maroon Bells; however, it is very dangerous and a guide is highly recommended.

see.name: Independence Pass
see.desc: In the summer months, this pass is open to vehicular traffic. The drive takes you up to the Continental Divide, and along the way passes some of the most beautiful scenery in the area and a ghost town that is open to visitors.

see.name: Belly Up
see.desc: Small venue hosting some impressive artists, downtown Aspen.

see.name: Jazz Aspen Snowmass Labor Day Festival
see.desc: Snowmass Town Park, the first weekend in September

see.name: Aspen Golf Club
see.desc: It opened with 9 holes in the early 1960s and expanded to 18 holes in the 1980s. The Aspen Golf Club facility features 7,114 yards of golf from the longest tees for a par of 71. The course has a rating of 73.8 and it has a slope rating of 139 from the tips. The course is primarily Blue grass and Poana.

see.name: Maroon Creek Club
see.desc: The 18-hole course at the Maroon Creek Club features 7,100 yards of golf from the longest tees for a par of 70. The course rating is 73.6 and it has a slope rating of 140 on Blue grass. The course opened in 1995.

see.name: Snowmass Club
see.desc: Ten minutes downvalley in Snowmass Village. The Snowmass Club's new 18-hole, par-72 Snowmass Club Golf Course. The 6,986-yard semi-private course designed by award-winning golf course architect Jim Engh includes a learning center, practice area and new golf clubhouse with Black Saddle Bar & Grille, a full-service restaurant and bar. With five sets of tee boxes at each hole and a truly unique design, golfers of all abilities will enjoy play that is as fun as it is challenging

see.name: River Valley Ranch Golf Club
see.desc: Eighteen holes, slope 73.2, rating 125, 7,348 yards. 30 minutes downvalley in Carbondale,River Valley Ranch Golf Club. Good bang for buck.

eat.name: The Artisan Restaurant
eat.desc: In Snowmass in the Stone Bridge Inn has a fresh menu and many off-menu options.

eat.name: Woody Creek Tavern
eat.desc: In "downtown" Woody Creek. Good for lunch, this is the former haunt of the late Hunter S. Thompson. It's about 15 miles from Aspen.

eat.name: The Pine Creek Cookhouse
eat.desc: It is worth the trip down a beautiful valley to the elegant log cabinesque building. Their food is very fresh, on the gourmet side, and not overly expensive. Reservations recommended. Highly recommended to stop in for lunch after a morning hike to one of the many great trails in the area such as Cathedral Lake.

eat.name: The Hickory House
eat.desc: Located on the bend towards the entrance to Aspen on Main Street. Tourists are often crowded out by the locals, drawn by fabulous barbecue and huge, hearty breakfasts. If you're lucky enough to be in Aspen for Thanksgiving (late November), turn out for annual Hickory House freebie: turkey, with all the trimmings, and all gratis.

eat.name: Ajax Tavern
eat.desc: Great apres-ski complete with the who's who of Aspen. Fantastic deck perfect for watching skiers come down the mountain while you enjoy people watching of the rich and famous. Order the Ajax Double Double, the best burger in town.

eat.name: J-Bar
eat.desc: The J-Bar is one of Aspen's favorite watering holes. Located at the luxurious Hotel Jerome

eat.name: Prospect
eat.desc: Prospect serves diverse Colorado cuisine with alpine influence prepared from wholesome natural ingredients. Breakfast, lunch and Sunday brunch.

eat.name: Syzygy
eat.desc: A trendy, favorite for many visitors.

eat.name: Pinions
eat.desc: Expensive, exquisite cuisine popular with celebrities and socialites.

eat.name: Campo De Fiori
eat.desc: Great Italian food that makes you feel like you're in Italy. Also has a great bar scene.

eat.name: Mezzaluna
eat.desc: Great Italian-American style food in a trendy establishment. Best place for lunch and late at night.

eat.name: Boogies Diner
eat.desc: Centrally located diner located in a jeans store.

eat.name: Paradise Bakery
eat.desc: Best ice cream in town, along with amazing baked goods and coffees. Located in central Aspen.

eat.name: Cloud-9 Bistro
eat.desc: Excellent European food on Aspen Highlands. Very well priced. Perfect for a ski day lunch break. Frequently visited by celebrities.

eat.name: Caribou Club
eat.desc: Insanely expensive and fancy private dining club for snobby locals.

eat.name: bb's kitchen
eat.desc: Classy but casual restaurant known for brunch, but also serves excellent dinner. Also has balcony seating.

eat.name: L'Hostaria
eat.desc: Well known Italian restaurant serving handmade pasta. Their bar features a bar menu with less expensive alternatives to the restaurant menu (in the bar menu, pasta entrees start around $12, and meat entrees start around $15).

eat.name: Grateful Deli
eat.desc: Good sandwiches, good-size portions for about $8 per sandwich

eat.name: Annette's Mountain Bake Shop
eat.desc: Baked goods and good sandwiches

eat.name: Peach's Corner Cafe
eat.desc: A busy place for breakfast, brunch, and lunch, featuring fresh and local food.

eat.name: Butcher's Block Deli
eat.desc: Good deli also known for its soup.

eat.name: Cache Cache
eat.desc: Excellent French restaurant is the trendy place to see and be seen. Their bar menu is excellent and offers a less expensive alternative (~$20 per entree) than the restaurant section. The bar starts to fill up around 6PM.

eat.name: Matsuhisia
eat.desc: Amazing and award-winning Japanese food along with some of the best sushi in the country.

see.name: Vallecito Lake
see.desc: This lake is one of the biggest and most beautiful bodies of water in all of Colorado. Located in the San Juan National Forest, there is breath taking scenery year-round

see.name: Durango Arts Center
see.desc: Exhibits a diversity of media and artists. Live performances, educational programs, and art classes.

see.name: Fort Lewis College
see.desc: Take in the “postcard view” of historic Durango and its surrounding valley and mountains by walking the Rim Trail or cruising Rim Drive, the road encircling the campus perimeter. McPherson Chapel, along the rim, is a favorite picnicking spot. Campus visitors also admire the college’s distinctive Mesa Verde-style architecture, numerous public art installations, and the Hesperus Peace Park

see.name: Purgatory at Durango Mountain Resort
see.desc: If you want a face to face experience with the San Juan Mountains head up 25 miles (40 km) north of town to Purgatory at Durango Mountain Resort. A ski area that has the glitzy feel like that of Aspen or Vail yet it still has a hometown local vibe with "The Beach" at the base where there is always music playing and people enjoying a beer while watching people ski and board down the slopes. With trails from beginner to expert this mountain is great for families and people of all ages. There are many shops and restaurants to choose from. You can go up for a day or stay at one of the many charming and classy condominiums. The best part of Durango Mountain Resort is that fun doesn't end when ski season does. There are tons of hiking and biking trails along with the Alpine Slide that entertains tourists and locals all summer long.

see.name: Durango & Silverton Narrow-Gauge Railroad
see.desc: This steam-gauge railroad is one of the great scenic railroad lines of the United States. The train runs round trip tours to the mountain town of [[Silverton (Colorado)

see.name: Historic Durango
see.desc: You can walk around and get the feel of the old West. Downtown Durango is home to historic boutique hotels and art galleries that feature paintings and sculptures of a Western theme, and shops where you can buy toy figures of cowboys, cowboy hats, and all articles of clothing that Durango images.

see.name: Rafting and Jeep Tours
see.desc: Wild Rafting & Jeep Tours offers half and full day excursions

see.name: Sky Ute Casino Resort
see.desc: Sky Ute Casino offers a Las Vegas style casino, dining, bowling, and entertainment.

see.name: Zipline
see.desc: Soaring Treetop Adventures offers an all-day, family-friendly zipline adventure in the Durango mountains that is fun and safe for all ages.

see.name: Rock Climb & Rappel
see.desc: Visit San Juan Expeditions and book a half or full day of climbing at the various Durango rock climbing sites.

see.name: Durango Arts Center
see.desc: Created and sustained by the people of the Four Corners region, the Durango Arts Center promotes the exploration, education, enrichment and enjoyment of the arts. The arts center offers plays, exhibits, and a shop.

eat.name: Serious Texas Bar-B-Q
eat.desc: Main location: 3535 North Main Avenue, +1 970 247-2240. Secondary location: 650 S Camino Del Rio, +1 970 259-9507. Daily 11AM-9PM. Excellent barbeque, with large portions and delicious food. The main location has a great atmosphere, with plenty of signs and memorabilia from Texas, without overloading you.

eat.name: Bar D Chuckwagon
eat.desc: Enjoy authentic Old West entertainment under the stars. After dinner the Bar D Wranglers take to the stage to entertain with their famous stage show of cowboy songs, poetry, and comedy.

eat.name: Gazpacho New Mexican Restaurant y Cantina
Steamworks Brewing Company
eat.desc: Award-winning beers that are brewed as you watch! Enjoy all the peanuts you can eat that come out before your meal. You can even throw the peanut shells on the ground! Fun for family and friends.

see.name: Peabody Museum of Natural History at Yale University
Yale University Art Gallery
see.desc: Chapel at High St. Tu-Sa 10AM-5PM, Th until 8PM from Sep-Jun, Su 1-6PM. Free.

see.name: Sterling Memorial Library at Yale University
see.desc: Includes the Yale Babylonian Collection donated by JP Morgan in 1910, and many other world-renowned artifacts and collections.

see.name: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library
see.desc: The Beinecke holds Yale's rare books and manuscripts. The building is impressive from outside, but particularly beautiful inside due to the glow that the translucent veined marble walls have on a sunny day. Rotating exhibits and a Gutenberg Bible are always on display.

see.name: The Green
see.desc: Public park in the center of the city. It's over 350 years old and recognized as one of the best 100 public spaces in the United States. Frequent festivals are held here.

see.name: Blessed Michael McGivney Pilgrimage Center (formerly Knights of Columbus Museum)
Lighthouse Point Park
see.desc: Lighthouse Point Park gives a scenic view of New Haven’s shoreline and is perfect for those looking to leave the hustle and bustle of the downtown area. The park is home to Hawkfest, a celebration of the local wildlife, and the Carousel at Lighthouse Point. Visit their website for department phone numbers, park opening times, and parking information.

see.name: Pardee Morris House
see.desc: Visit a landmark of colonial New Haven. Built in 1750 and burned down in 1779 during a British raid on New Haven Harbor, the Pardee Morris House offers a glimpse into New Haven’s history. Classes, tours, and summer camps are held throughout the year. Visit the Pardee Morris House section of the New Haven Museums website for a schedule of events.

see.name: Fort Nathan Hale Park
see.desc: Get a spectacular view of the New Haven seaside as well as learn about the town’s colonial history. See Black Rock Fort, replete with the Betsy Ross flag, and take in a recreation of battles from New Haven’s past. Fish from its expansive pier or take the nature trail that leads from the park to the Pardee Seawall. The visitor center is open from Memorial Day to Labor Day from 10AM to 4PM. Visit their website for more information.

see.name: Leitner Family Observatory and Planetarium at Yale University
see.desc: Shows in the planetarium theater on Tuesday nights, followed by viewing of the night sky through telescopes (weather permitting). Check website for current shows, as well as special events on other nights.

see.name: Amistad Memorial
see.desc: Depicting the slave trader Joseph Cinqué, commonly known as Sengbe Pieh, this 14-foot bronze sculpture commemorates the events of the Amistad Affair of 1839, which was a kidnapping of 53 Mende captives, who led the revolt aboard the ''La Amistad'', a two-masted schooner. It sits in front of a city hall, where the slaves were imprisoned during their trial.

see.name: Long Wharf Theatre
see.desc: Not only are some of the best plays in the North East performed right on this stage, the theater also gives back to the community by hosting classes and sessions for those interested in theater and want to get involved in the performing arts.

eat.name: Libbys Italian Cookies and Pastries
eat.desc: Amazing cookies, cannoli, Italian pastries, Italian ice, and coffee.

eat.name: Louis' Lunch
eat.desc: This tiny hamburger joint, a few blocks off the Green, claims to be the inventor of the hamburger. The burger served in Louis' traditional style: steamed in an antique table-top cast-iron gas broiler, served between two pieces of white-bread toast, optionally with cheese, tomato, and onion. Condiments like ketchup, mayonnaise, and mustard are ''not'' used or available, which is a point of pride for management who are adamant that such extras detract from the experience. Sides such as potato salad, chips, pies, and local Foxon Park soda are available. Do not expect McDonald's wait times for your burger!

eat.name: Aladdin Crown Pizza
eat.desc: Don't be fooled by the name; the best cuisine this place offers is not pizza; it's Middle Eastern. Be sure to try their falafel plate and baclava dessert. Authentic food with excellent service.

eat.name: Claire's Corner Copia
eat.desc: Vegan and vegetarian options, regularly-changing specials. Known for their Lithuanian coffee cake. Great bakery with gluten-free options. Kosher.

eat.name: Pacifico
eat.desc: Latin American seafood dishes with an upscale New York sensibility served at this LGBT-friendly restaurant.

eat.name: Union League Café
eat.desc: Upscale French cuisine. Make reservations.

eat.name: York St. Noodle House
eat.desc: If you're looking for an inexpensive, casual meal, York St. Noodle House is the place to go. Service is always friendly, and the menu always has irresistible options. Be sure to try their delicious boba fruit slushy. Try also coconut curry noodle soup and spicy wok basil noodle.

eat.name: Yorkside Pizza and Restaurant
eat.desc: Family-owned diner with large menu and very reasonable prices. Dough and sauces are made fresh daily on the premises.

eat.name: Zinc
eat.desc: Modern American. Chef's table options focus on local food items. Make reservations.

eat.name: Encore by Goodfellas
eat.desc: This is the perfect place not only for the connoisseur of Italian cuisine but for also a lover of movies. You can enjoy some of the finest Italian food New Haven has to offer while viewing movie classics on their ten flatscreen televisions

eat.name: Brazi's Italian Restaurant
eat.desc: Italian-American foods made with the freshest ingredients, salads, desserts. Dining, bar and banquet room.

eat.name: Modern Apizza
eat.desc: This New Haven-style apizza place has really stirred up the waters of New Haven cuisine, dethroning the seemingly invincible Pepe's and Sally's as the city's (and quite possibly the world's) best pizza place. Modern Apizza has been voted "Best Pizza" in New Haven for 12 consecutive years in the New Haven Advocate’s "Best of" Reader’s Poll. Modern Apizza is a long walk, or a short drive, bike ride or trip on the "M" bus from Downtown New Haven.

eat.name: Prime 16
eat.desc: 16 taps of craft beer, accompanied by imaginative burgers

eat.name: Willoughby's
eat.desc: Locally roasted coffee. The to-go tumblers are reusable and a great deal.

see.name: Connecticut State Capitol
see.desc: Downtown atop Bushnell Park the capitol is a National Historic Landmark that opened back in 1878. This stunning building is made of marble and is topped off by a gold dome. Open for free on-hour tours year round.

see.name: Bushnell Park
see.desc: The first publicly funded park in America. Located in the center of the city and bordering the state capitol building. The park was designed by the architect of Central Park in New York City.

see.name: Wadsworth Atheneum
see.desc: America's first public art museum, founded in 1842. The Wadsworth has more than 45,000 works of art as part of its permanent collection. Free admission during final hour (4-5PM) $20/adult, $15/senior, $10/student, children free.

see.name: Connecticut Science Center
see.desc: With 150 hands-on exhibits, a state-of-the-art 3D digital theater, four educational labs, plus daily programs and events, the Connecticut Science Center offers endless exploration for children, teens and adults.

see.name: Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Arch
see.desc: The first permanent triumphal arch and the first permanent war memorial in America, it pays tribute to the Connecticut soldiers who lost their lives in the American Civil War. It also pays tribute to slaves and their struggle. The iconic arch was dedicated on September 17, 1886.

see.name: Old State House
see.desc: Downtown. The original Connecticut Capitol building is a National Historic Landmark that dates back to 1796 making it one of the oldest state houses in the country.

see.name: Elizabeth Park
see.desc: Elizabeth Park is on the national register of historic places. Elizabeth Park offers just over one hundred acres of formal gardens, green space, recreational facilities, walking loops, and the Pond House Café. Come enjoy the beauty of the gardens and grounds.

see.name: Mark Twain House & Museum
see.desc: Located in the city's historic Asylum Hill neighborhood, this is where popular author Mark Twain lived from 1874-1891. During this time Twain wrote many famous books, including ''The Adventures of Tom Sawyer'' and the ''Adventures of Huckleberry Finn''. Built in the high Victorian Gothic style, this home has been fabulously restored and offers an enlightening insight into the family life of one of America's favorite authors. The accompanying Visitors Center offers an additional educational perspective relative to the issues of Twain's day.

see.name: Harriet Beecher Stowe House & Library
see.desc: This is the historic home of Harriet Beecher Stowe, who is best known for being the author of ''Uncle Tom's Cabin.'' The Stowe's moved in this house in 1873, one year before Mark Twain moved in next door.

see.name: Butler McCook House & Garden
see.desc: Downtown. The oldest home in the city that dates back to 1782. Also home of the city's oldest collection of art, antiques and household items. The site also includes a wonderful restored garden.

see.name: Connecticut Historical Society Museum & Library
see.desc: In the West End the Connecticut Historical Society is one of the oldest historical societies in the country and has one of the greatest library and museum collections in New England.

see.name: The Governor's Residence
see.desc: Located in the city's West End neighborhood the governor's mansion was built back in 1909 and has been the home of governor's and their families since 1943. The 15,000 square foot (1,400 m2) residence is on 4 acres (1.6 hectares) and has 9 fireplaces, nine bathrooms, a pool and is a National Historic Landmark. Guided tours can be arranged.

see.name: Colt Factory
see.desc: Hartford. America's favorite gun shop, shaped like an Arabian palace. It can be viewed just south of the skyline from East Hartford. It is in Hartford's south end.

see.name: XL Center
see.desc: The largest arena in Connecticut. This is the former home of the Hartford Whalers National Hockey League team and numerous other professional sports teams and the current home of American Hockey League Hartford Wolfpack, and one of two homes for the men's and women's basketball programs of the University of Connecticut Huskies, and for its men’s hockey program. Various bands and recording artists perform here, mostly popular and more established acts.

see.name: Bushnell Center for the Performing Arts
see.desc: Hartford (Downtown). The state's premier performing arts theater. Home of the ''Hartford Symphony Orchestra'' and ''Connecticut Opera''. Principally showcases classical music and traveling Broadway shows. Popular comics also tour here.

see.name: Xfinity Theatre
see.desc: Hartford (North Meadows - just north of Downtown). This is a huge amphitheater that has 6,100 seats in a covered pavilion and a lawn that can hold up to 18,000 people. The Center brings in big name concerts each year including the Dave Mattews Band, Britney Spears, O.A.R., Weezer, John Mayer, Pearl Jam and Aerosmith. The Center is closed in the winter months but is open the rest of the year.
see.alt: formerly New England Dodge Music Center

see.name: Connecticut Convention Center
see.desc: At 540,000 square feet (50,000 m2), the largest convention center in southern New England overlooks the Connecticut River and downtown. Hosts tons of national and local conventions, events, meetings, dinners, etc. each year. Attached to the center is the 409-room, 22-story Marriott Hartford Hotel Downtown.

see.name: Hartford Stage
see.desc: Tony award-winning theatre that constantly puts on shows and takes in shows from on-the-road Broadway plays. Usually produces six major productions annually and one or two summer productions each year.

see.name: Dunkin' Park
see.desc: Baseball stadium, home of the Hartford Yard Goats minor league baseball.

see.name: Dillon Stadium
see.desc: Stadium, home of the Hartford Athletic soccer team.

see.name: Pratt & Whitney Stadium
see.desc: East Hartford. An awesome stadium completed in 2003 that is the home of University of Connecticut Football. The stadium is also used as a concert hall and has hosted big names like Bruce Springsteen, the Rolling Stones and The Police. Overall the stadium sits on 75 acres (30 hectares) and has 40,000 seats.

see.name: Cinestudio
see.desc: An independent theater on the campus of Trinity College that shows classic, art house and second run films. The theater is open to the public and has been showing films since its founding in 1970.

see.name: Art Cinema
see.desc: Built in 1919 in the south end this is the city's last operating movie house. The theater used to be known as the Rialto and changed names in the 1950s when it started showing art films.

see.name: Webster Theater
see.desc: Voted the best rock club and best place to see live music for the past five years by the Hartford Advocate. The art deco theater has been fully renovated features everything from a movie screen to five different bars.

see.name: Real Art Ways
see.desc: One of the country’s early multi-disciplinary “alternative spaces,” Real Art Ways has evolved to become a leading center for contemporary art and ideas. Programming covers a broad range of cultural activities including visual arts exhibitions, concerts, literary readings, education and family programs, public art, community projects, and daily cinema screenings.

see.name: Ski Sundown
see.desc: A great place for beginner and intermediate skiers, about 40 minutes west of Hartford, in Northwestern Connecticut.

see.name: Sea Tea Comedy Theater
see.desc: It has improv shows and comedy shows. Also, there are family-friendly shows every Sunday from 2PM to 4PM.

eat.name: Bear's Smokehouse Barbecue
eat.desc: Opened in 2014, brings southern-style BBQ to the neighborhood.

eat.name: Black-Eyed Sally's Southern Kitchen & Bar
eat.desc: Serves BBQ and Cajun restaurant southeastern food. The restaurant also plays live music from many well-known and local blues artists.

eat.name: El Pollo Guapo
eat.desc: A neighborhood rotisserie joint featuring whole roasted chickens, fresh sides, tacos and salads.

eat.name: Salute
eat.desc: Trendy Italian restaurant with an upscale menu of pastas (gluten-free available) & grilled dishes.

eat.name: Fire-N-Spice Vegan Restaurant
eat.desc: Vegan restaurant.

eat.name: Le Petit Chef
eat.desc: French restaurant, sandwiches.

eat.name: Cornerstone
eat.desc: Deli, Sandwich shop.

eat.name: The Brownstone
eat.desc: Pizza, bar. Local branch of a small chain that started in [[Manhattan/East Village

eat.name: Kravin Pho
eat.desc: Pho & other Vietnamese specialties.

eat.name: Han Restaurant
eat.desc: Sichuan cuisine.

eat.name: ON20
eat.desc: Fine dining restaurant. Acclaimed New American fare in an elegant, urbane space on the 20th floor with city & river views.

eat.name: The Capital Grille
eat.desc: Fine dining restaurant. Outpost of the upscale steakhouse chain offers classic American fare and a clubby, refined setting.

eat.name: Max Downtown
eat.desc: Fine dining restaurant. Upscale spot with prime cuts & seafood, extensive wine list, cocktails for expense account crowd.

eat.name: Máncora Restobar
eat.desc: Peruvian cuisine.

eat.name: Mozzicato De Pasquale Bakery & Pastry Shop
Vaughan's Public House
eat.desc: Cozy pub offering traditional Irish fare, Guinness & single malts amid dark woods & memorabilia.

eat.name: Pig’s Eye Pub
eat.desc: Famous for never having a cover, and live bands on the roof top patio. Overall a rowdy little place with lots of fun.

eat.name: Black-Eyed Sally's
eat.desc: Southern fare & BBQ in a hip, vibrant roadhouse with live blues, jazz & soul music.

eat.name: Arch Street Tavern
eat.desc: Historic restaurant/bar featuring a rustic atmosphere, pub food and live music.

eat.name: Agave Grill
eat.desc: Upscale tequila bar, quieter and more mature. Features an excellent selection of tequila and also serves up great Mexican cuisine.

eat.name: Spigot Cafe
eat.desc: Laid-back bar with wide selection of draft and bottled beers.

see.name: Mystic Aquarium and Institute for Exploration
see.desc: Indoor and outdoor exhibits and habitats which cover a wide range of reptilian, amphibian, and aquatic species. Examples of exhibits include the beluga whale exhibit, penguin exhibit, and sea lion exhibit. In addition, there are many tanks containing coral, sharks, reef-fish, stingrays, and other creatures. Some exhibits are also interactive, such as the shark and ray “touch-pools.” Amongst these exhibits are a number of special events like the daily Marine Theater shows.

see.name: Mystic Seaport - The Museum of America and the Sea
see.desc: The nation's largest maritime museum. A [[living history museum]] on 17 acres. Old historic port used in the filming of many movies, including Amistad.

see.name: Denison Pequotsepos Nature Center
see.desc: Open year round, this natural history museum and live animal exhibits display Connecticut’s local habitats; great for kids.

see.name: Mystic Ballet
see.desc: Local ballet company that puts on regular performances and acts throughout the year.

see.name: Steamboat Sabino at Mystic Seaport
see.desc: The oldest, wooden, coal-fired steamboat still in operation offers historic views along the scenic Mystic River.

see.name: B.F. Clyde’s Cider Mill
see.desc: View an engineering relic at work while enjoying some of the freshest cider around; also enjoy famous “hard” ciders of various types.

see.name: Argia Mystic Cruises
see.desc: Three or four sails daily (2 hr; subject to cancellation in bad weather or if there are too few customers) May–mid-Oct aboard a traditional schooner. See historic Mystic Harbor, Mystic River, islands, and lighthouses. Public sails or charter the whole boat.

see.name: Benmar Custom Charters
see.desc: Hatteras Charter fishing boat licensed in three states and federal waters.

see.name: Brilliant
see.desc: Sail this 62-foot schooner, built in 1932. Day trips and longer voyages. Customers do participate in the sailing, especially on the longer voyages. There are 5- and 10-day programs specifically for teens. Most sailings sell out.

see.name: Denison Pequotsepos Nature Center
see.desc: Explore woodland, wetland and meadow habitats on eight miles of trails on a 250-acre wildlife sanctuary.

see.name: Mystic Whaler Cruises
see.desc: The Mystic Whaler is a 93' tall ship that takes passengers out on day sails, lobster dinner cruises and multi-day vacation cruises. Just 10 miles away from Mystic, this schooner offers a variety of all age sailing adventures.

see.name: Olde Mystick Village Art Cinemas
see.desc: Watch the artistic films not being played anywhere else. View many films the way the director intended them to be viewed. A very interesting and profound way to spend an afternoon.

eat.name: Abbott's Lobster in the Rough
eat.desc: If you visit Mystic during the summer and have adequate transportation, be sure to eat here. A classic New England seafood restaurant, Abbott's opens in May for the summer. You may BYOB and enjoy fresh seafood at market price.

eat.name: Anthony J's
eat.desc: A classic Italian bistro featuring imported pasta and some American fare. Be sure to explore the wine selection.

eat.name: Bravo, Bravo & Bar
eat.desc: Fine Italian dining for $20-25.

eat.name: Go Fish
eat.desc: Olde Mistick Village, 23 Coogan Boulevard. M-Th 11:30AM-9:30PM, F Sa 11:30AM-10PM, Su noon-9:30PM. Enjoy the best seafood in Mystic anyway you like it; cooked or raw for an experience at the sushi bar.

eat.name: Kitchen Little
eat.desc: (Route 27). A small shack-like building on your way into Mystic. This has the best breakfast around. The service is friendly and they are quick to refill your java. The sausage and home fries are great and so is the charm. Dining inside is packed tight with tables, but your reward will be worth the squeeze. They offer loads of vegetarian options but very little (other than a veggie wrap around lunch) for vegans. Under $10 for a hearty breakfast.

eat.name: Mystic Pizza
eat.desc: No Julia Roberts doesn't work there; you can check out the sweet 1988 romantic comedy if you want to see her dish up something nice. Otherwise this is your go-to spot for tourist grub. Enjoy at under $20 for entree or pizza.

eat.name: Mezza Mediterranean Cuisine
eat.desc: Rt. 1. An interesting alternative for a dining experience in Mystic, The Pita Spot boasts a Mediterranean menu unlike any other in the area. Enjoy an American breakfast, or a Mediterranean lunch and dinner outside during the summer, or inside during the winter. A tourist hot-spot, The Pita Spot is small and cozy with service that will tend to your every need.

eat.name: S&P Oyster Co
eat.desc: Close to many of Mystic's attractions, this restaurant draws crowds for its fantastic seafood. In the summertime, diners can sit on the outdoor patio and enjoy the seaport. $20-30.

eat.name: Steak Loft
eat.desc: Fine dining and an olde tyme atmosphere. Voted Connecticut magazine "Best Steak", and rightfully so! Expect to pay about $25 for their top-rated steaks.

eat.name: The Captain Daniel Packer Inne, Restaurant and Pub
eat.desc: Built over 250 years ago, this restaurant is two stories. The lower floor is a small pub, the upper story is a restaurant. They have two different menus, both excellent. Particularly good, and reasonably priced, are the fish and chips and burgers in the pub. Arrive early to get a table in the pub section. If none are available, the more expensive restaurant section is also worth the visit.

eat.name: Angies Pizza
eat.desc: Enjoy the expansive Greek menu of this local hotspot. This quiet yet bustling restaurant has extremely reliable service and quality. A very relaxed dining experience.

eat.name: Mystic Drawbridge Ice Cream
eat.desc: Next to the bridge that is part of its namesake, this small ice cream parlor serves a varied menu of frozen treats with something for everyone. Open during Summer and Winter, their menu includes a wide spectrum of choices from salads and sandwiches to ice cream, malts, and pastries. Their ice cream offerings include over 25 varieties, made with a number of local ingredients.

eat.name: Mystic Market East
eat.desc: Just outside the downtown area, Mystic Market provides both made-fresh deli dishes as well as other sundries. Their dishes can be both packaged to bring home or eaten at their window-side bistro tables. Amongst the items offered on the menu that can be found on their site are wraps, paninis, salads, sandwiches, and coffees.

eat.name: Captain Daniel Packer Inn (DPI)
eat.desc: Enjoy the nightly entertainment in the cozy pub downstairs. Must be 21 or older to enter.

eat.name: Harp and Hound
eat.desc: An authentic Irish pub serving up an assortment of beers. Yes they have Guinness on tap! Great atmosphere. Must be 21 or older to enter.

eat.name: John's Cafe
eat.desc: Good place to go and watch the big games. Must be 21 or older to enter.

eat.name: Margaritas
eat.desc: The "watering hole" above the restaurant brings the feeling and energy of Mexico to the community. Must be 21 or older to enter.

see.name: Anna Hazzard Museum
see.desc: Museum offering artifacts and memorabilia documenting local history in a camp meeting home from 1895.

see.name: Nanticoke Indian Museum
see.desc: Native American library and artifacts documenting the history of the Nanticoke Indians.

see.name: Rehoboth Beach Historical Society Museum
see.desc: Museum showcasing the history of Rehoboth Beach. Artifacts include vintage postcards, bathing suits, photos, and souvenirs.

see.name: Central Park
see.desc: Natural wooded area with pine, oak, and magnolia trees. Trails offer views of deer, birds, and native wildlife.

see.name: Cranberry Park
see.desc: A small park with benches for a quiet respite.

see.name: Deauville Beach Tennis Courts
see.desc: Four tennis Courts are available in the Deuville Beach parking lot, just northeast of the North Surf Avenue and Henlopen Avenue intersection.

see.name: Deer Park
see.desc: Natural wooded area with pine, oak, and magnolia trees.

see.name: Grove Park
see.desc: Located near the Visitor Center and Museum, Grove Park has a “Tot Lot” and a ten station circuit training work out area. There is one large pavilion, one smaller picnic pavilion, bathrooms and a drinking fountain. From May to October, Grove Park hosts The Rehoboth Beach Farmer's Market on Tuesdays from noon to four.

see.name: Lake Gerar Park
see.desc: Lake Gerar Park is located on Lake Avenue near but not on the ocean. There is a "Tot Lot" for small children and benches on which to view the lake. At the west end of the lake, there is a small fishing deck.

see.name: Lee Street Park
see.desc: A small park with trees to provide shade.

see.name: Martin's Lawn
see.desc: A small park next to the Anna Hazzard Museum and Senior Center with a grassy area and crape myrtle trees.

see.name: Stockley Street Park
see.desc: Located along Silver Lake, this park offers a "Tot Lot" along with a foot bridge over the lake from which you can feed the ducks, turtles, and carp.

see.name: Baywood Greens
see.desc: Called the "Augusta of the North", Baywood Greens is an 18-hole championship public golf course surrounded by gardens.

see.name: Clear Space Theatre
see.desc: Theater company near the boardwalk that provides live performances six nights a week.

see.name: Delmarva Board Sports
see.desc: Delmarva Board Sports offers kayak and paddle board rentals along with lessons and excursions.

see.name: Funland
see.desc: Family-oriented amusement park on the boardwalk that has children's rides along with an arcade featuring skee ball and roller derby.

see.name: Junction and Breakwater Trail
see.desc: Scenic trail for hikers and bicyclists connecting Rehoboth Beach and Lewes.

see.name: Jungle Jim's River Safari Water Park
see.desc: The largest waterpark in Delaware featuring slides and bumper boats.

see.name: Midway Par 3 Golf Course & Driving Range
see.desc: Golf course offering par 3 holes and a driving range.

see.name: Midway Speedway Park
see.desc: Fun park that features go-kart tracks, miniature golf, and the White Water Mountain Water Park.

see.name: Movies at Midway
see.desc: Movie theater situated along Rte 1 near the Tanger Outlets showing new releases. A great place to go on a rainy day at the beach.

see.name: Rehoboth Beach Bandstand
see.desc: Bandstand that offers free entertainment, with the Summer Concert Series offering performances from over 50 bands during the course of the summer.

see.name: Rehoboth Surf Boarding School
see.desc: Sport tour agency that offers surfing lessons and rentals.

see.name: Heritage Inn & Suites Rehoboth Beach
see.desc: Spacious rooms, pet-friendly.

eat.name: Grotto Pizza
eat.desc: A Delaware favorite, Grotto Pizza is a modestly-priced local pizza chain known for pizza with a swirl of sauce on top. Also features a bar area. Grotto Pizza has two locations on the Rehoboth Beach boardwalk and one along Rehoboth Avenue

eat.name: Victoria's Restaurant
eat.desc: Located inside the Boardwalk Plaza Hotel, serves (slightly pricey) breakfast daily and weekend brunch. By putting their own, exciting twist on classic favorites, Victoria's has come up with delicacies like Raspberry Swirl French Toast and a Cinnamon Apple Crepe. Reservations for brunch are recommended.

eat.name: Double Dippers
eat.desc: Old-fashioned ice cream parlor. Over 40 flavors of Hersheys ice cream. Soft serve as well. Shakes, malts, floats, old-fashioned sodas, sundaes and banana splits. Huge scoops and friendly sit down service.

eat.name: Go Fish!
eat.desc: It's a small, slightly cramped little place, and the prices are a little high, but the fish and chips are absolutely spot on, they have good ales on tap, friendly and efficient service, plus they are right around the corner from the heart of the boardwalk. The fried sausages (made by some British expat in town exclusively for the restaurant) are a real treat, as is the sticky toffee pudding.

eat.name: Big Oyster Brewery
eat.desc: Brewery within Fins Ale House and Raw Bar that brews IPAs and lagers.

eat.name: Dogfish Head Brewery and Eats
eat.desc: A craft brewery/distillery with fun, out-of-the-ordinary beers, spirits, and food. From "Ginger Peach Wheat" beer to wood-grilled pizzas, to the stacked indulgence burger, you are guaranteed a pretty decadent meal. Service is pretty unimpressive, but in fairness, it is a big noisy place and they still get the job done efficiently. To get a behind-the-scenes look at how they brew their beer, DFH invites guests to take a free tour every Wednesday at 5PM. Outdoor seating available. Prices are really a steal.

eat.name: Revelations Craft Brewery
eat.desc: Local brewery.

see.name: The Brandywine Zoo
see.desc: Fun for the whole family. You can take the #2 DART First State bus from the Amtrak station to the zoo.

see.name: Delaware Art Museum
see.desc: Art museum showcasing exhibits from established and emerging Delaware artists, featuring paintings, sculptures, photography, and crafts. Free on Sundays.

see.name: Delaware History Museum
see.desc: Museum showcasing the history and heritage of Delaware, featuring interactive exhibits.

see.name: Hagley Museum and Library
see.desc: Museum and library on the banks of the Brandywine Creek at the site of the DuPont family's gunpowder mill and first home and garden. Open for tours.

see.name: Nemours Mansion & Gardens
see.desc: DuPont family country estate that is modeled after Versailles, consisting of a mansion, gardens, artwork, and sculptures.

see.name: Rockwood Park & Museum
see.desc: Park centered around an English-style country estate and museum that was built between 1851 and 1854 and serves as an example of Rural Gothic Revival Architecture.

see.name: The Delaware Contemporary
see.alt: formerly Delaware Center for the Contemporary Arts

see.name: Delaware Park
see.desc: Delaware Park consists of a thoroughbred race track, casino, and golf course located to the south of Wilmington. The race track offers seasonal thoroughbred racing in along with simulcasts of races from other tracks year-round. The casino at Delaware Park has table games and over 2,500 slot machines on two levels. There is also keno and betting on professional and college sports. Delaware Park offers casual and fine dining options including Legends Restaurant, Picciotti's Pizza and Craft Beer, Del Cap Room, At The Rail Wine Bar and Grille, On A Roll Deli, Rooney's, Kelso's Coffee Shop, New Castle Room, Sports Book, The Grove at Delaware Park, and The Terrace. Delaware Park also has facilities to accommodate banquets. Bars at Delaware Park include Paddock Pub, Hops, Oval Bar, and Wheel Bar. Delaware Park offers an 18-hole public golf course.

see.name: Delaware Theater Company
see.desc: Local theater company in a small riverfront theater that is home to a professional acting group that performs classic, modern, and youth plays.

see.name: Playhouse on Rodney Square (formerly The DuPont Theater)
see.desc: Inside the Hotel Du Pont.

see.name: Grand Opera House
see.desc: 19th-century opera house offering a diverse selection of performances from opera to ballet that is home to the '''[http://www.delawaresymphony.org/ Delaware Symphony Orchestra]''' and '''[http://www.operade.org/ Opera Delaware]'''.

see.name: Rock Manor Golf Club
see.desc: Public links.

see.name: Wilmington and Western Railroad
see.desc: The Wilmington and Western Railroad offers steam and diesel-powered excursions along the scenic Red Clay Creek between Greenbank and Hockessin. Excursion trains operate on weekends round-trip from Greenbank station to Hockessin for a 2½-hour trip, with a 30-minute layover in Hockessin, or round-trip from Greenbank station to the Mt. Cuba Picnic Grove for a 1½-hour trip, with a 30-minute layover allowing for a picnic. Several themed rides are offered throughout the year including the Easter Bunny Express, Fireworks Express, Back Burner Dinner Train, Brews on Board, Civil War Skirmish Weekend, Great Train Robbery, Murder on the Red Clay Express, Autumn Leaf Special, Halloween Express, Holiday Lights Express, and Santa Claus Express.

eat.name: River Rock Kitchen
eat.desc: Inspired by local ingredients, providing the freshest flavors of the season, River Rock Kitchen is a multi-occasion gathering place for a power breakfast, lunch with business associates or friends, and socializing over drinks and dinner.

eat.name: Capriotti's Sandwich Shop
eat.desc: Original location of sub shop that, since opening in 1976, has expanded into eleven states.

eat.name: Charcoal Pit
eat.desc: This local institution, and favorite of former President Joe Biden, has been serving up burgers, cheesesteaks and milkshakes since opening in 1956, and offers ice cream sundaes named for local high school mascots along with the "Kitchen Sink" sundae.

eat.name: Grotto Pizza
eat.desc: A Delaware favorite, Grotto Pizza is a modestly-priced local pizza chain known for pizza with a swirl of sauce on top. Grotto Pizza has two locations in Wilmington.

eat.name: Harry's Savoy Grill
eat.desc: Upscale American cuisine.

eat.name: Mikimotos
eat.desc: Upscale Japanese cuisine. Pricey.

eat.name: Mazzella's Italian Restaurant
eat.desc: Family owned pizzeria.

eat.name: Mrs. Robino's
eat.desc: Little Italy institution open since 1940.

eat.name: Walter's Steakhouse & Saloon
eat.desc: Well-known for their prime rib.

eat.name: Yi Palace
eat.desc: Chinese.

eat.name: Catherine Rooney's
eat.desc: Meat and potatoes Irish bar.

eat.name: Iron Hill Brewery
eat.desc: Newark-based brewpub chain's large Riverfront location.

eat.name: Kelly's Logan House
eat.desc: This Trolley Square tavern opened in 1864 and is a popular watering hole for young professionals.

see.name: Air Mobility Command Museum
see.desc: The museum is on the Dover Air Force Base. It is one of the only museums that is dedicated to airlift and air refueling. There are both indoor and outdoor exhibits, an ATC tower, and a 9/11 memorial.

see.name: Biggs Museum of American Art
see.desc: Museum housing a collection of American fine and decorative art, including furniture, paintings, silver, glass, ceramics, and textiles, 1700 to the present day.

see.name: Delaware Agricultural Museum and Village
see.desc: The agricultural museum, in a historic village set in the 1890s, is dedicated to helping kids remember where we came from. They offer tours for big or small groups.

see.name: Delaware Public Archives
see.desc: Public archives allowing for the viewing of historic collections and exhibits.

see.name: Delaware State Police Museum
see.desc: Museum showcasing the history of the Delaware State Police from 1920, featuring several exhibits.

see.name: First State Heritage Park
see.desc: An urban "park without boundaries," First State Heritage Park contains several historic sites in Dover including the Old State House, the Biggs Museum of American Art, and Legislative Hall. Special tours available on the first Saturday of each month.

see.name: The Green
see.desc: Public square that was laid out in 1717 and was the site of where Delaware became the first state to ratify the U.S. Constitution. Guided tours available.

see.name: John Dickinson Plantation
see.desc: The plantation house dating back to 1740 served as the home of American Revolution leader John Dickinson and recreates life in the 1700s.

see.name: Johnson Victorla Museum
see.desc: Museum documenting Eldridge Reeves Johnson, the founder of the Victor Talking Machine Company, featuring paintings, objects, memorabilia, and trademarks that highlight the development of the sound recording industry.

see.name: Legislative Hall
see.desc: The state capitol building of Delaware and home to the Delaware General Assembly, tours of the building are offered.

see.name: Old State House Museum
see.desc: Located on The Green, the Old State House was built from 1787 to 1792 and served as the seat of the state government from 1792 to 1932. Guided tours are available.

see.name: St. Jones Reserve
see.desc: Nature reserve along the St. Jones River with hiking trails, interactive activities, and exhibits.

see.name: Woodburn - The Governor's House
see.desc: A Middle Georgian house dating back to 1790, Woodburn has been the official residence of the Governor of Delaware since the state acquired the house in 1965. Tours are offered with 24-hour advance notice.

see.name: Bally's Dover Casino Resort
see.desc: The Dover Downs complex consists of a hotel, casino, and a harness racetrack. The hotel offers upscale accommodations with a full-service spa, indoor pool, fitness room, room service, and concierge. Rooms offer either a view of the racetrack or the city and have many amenities including pillow-top bedding, safe, free internet and voicemail, refrigerator, coffee maker, hair dryer, make-up mirror, and an iron and ironing board. Rooms are ADA compliant. The casino offers various games including over 2,300 slots, table games such as baccarat, roulette, and blackjack, and an 18-table poker room. The racetrack offers live harness racing from November to April along with simulcasts of races from other tracks year-round. The Race & Sports Book offers sports betting on horse racing along with professional and college sports. Bally's offers entertainment options ranging from comedians to singers, plus bars and restaurants. The Colonnade offers upscale shopping options including Fashions of the Colonnade, Godiva, Swarovski, The Colonnade Marketplace, and Sweet Perks Too.

see.name: Dover Motor Speedway
see.desc: Nicknamed the "Monster Mile", Dover Motor Speedway hosts a NASCAR race weekend in July, featuring the ARCA Menards Series race on Friday, the NASCAR Xfinity Series race on Saturday, and the NASCAR Cup Series race on Sunday. Aside from the racing activity on the track, Dover Motor Speedway features a FanZone that offers a number of activities, live music, and driver appearances. The FanZone is centered around the Monster Monument in Victory Plaza, a statue of the track's mascot Miles the Monster. Dover Motor Speedway offers both standard RV and tent camping along with Carefree Camping, where campers are provided with a tent that has a bed with linens, chairs, a table, and a rug. Additional RV and tent camping is available off premises.

see.name: Firefly Music Festival
see.desc: Four-day open-air music festival held in the middle of June at The Woodlands at Dover International Speedway, attracting nationally known music acts. The festival includes seven stages and offers outdoor camping.

see.name: Kent County Theatre Guild
see.desc: A local theater which offers shows throughout the year.

eat.name: 9 East Taphouse
eat.desc: A spacious, wood-paneled causal American restaurant offering views of Silver Lake. Banquet rooms available.

eat.name: Hollywood Diner
eat.desc: A classic American diner.

eat.name: Restaurant 55
eat.desc: American restaurant serving gourmet burgers and a selection of craft brewed ales.

eat.name: Bangkok Thai Cuisine
eat.desc: Restaurant specializing in Thai cuisine.

eat.name: Flavor of India
eat.desc: Indian restaurant serving exciting dishes and offering unique ambience.

eat.name: Hibachi Japanese Steak House
eat.desc: Japanese restaurant with food prepared by master chefs.

eat.name: Rice Restaurant
eat.desc: Restaurant serving Chinese-Japanese fusion cuisine, including sushi.

eat.name: Yukon Korean Barbecue & Sushi Bar
eat.desc: Asian restaurant serving fresh sushi and other Japanese and Korean dishes.

eat.name: Angelo's Pizza
eat.desc: Restaurant serving New York-style thin crust pizza.

eat.name: Capriotti's Sandwich Shop
eat.desc: Local sandwich shop chain serving subs and steak sandwiches. The Bobbie sandwich is a local favorite.

eat.name: Grotto Pizza
eat.desc: A Delaware favorite, Grotto Pizza is a modestly-priced local pizza chain known for pizza with a swirl of sauce on top. Also features a sports bar.

eat.name: Pizza Delight by Giacomo
eat.desc: Restaurant serving authentic Italian cuisine and fresh dough pizza.

eat.name: Roma Italian Restaurant
eat.desc: Italian restaurant offering a fine dining experience.

eat.name: Roma Pizza
eat.desc: Restaurant serving a wide selection of pizza, sandwiches, and desserts.

eat.name: La Hacienda
eat.desc: Mexican restaurant featuring a full bar with margaritas.

eat.name: McGlynns Pub and Restaurant
eat.desc: Has same owners as Deer Park Tavern in Newark, Delaware. McGlynns Pub is an Irish alehouse serving burgers and more and has a nice sit down area that is family friendly, and a bar area that has a very high spirited atmosphere. McGlynns Pub is a lively and active bar that boasts a great selection of beers, liquors, and wines, with TVs visible from most seats and sports games on them most of the time. The pub features Sunday brunch and trivia.

eat.name: Simaron Pizza & Steak Shop
eat.desc: Casual, down-home restaurant serving pizza, wings, hot and cold sandwiches, steaks, and Italian dishes.

eat.name: Cool Springs Fish Bar & Restaurant
eat.desc: Modern seafood restaurant featuring an open kitchen and colorful decor.

eat.name: Sambo's Tavern
eat.desc: Located in nearby Leipsic, rustic pub serving local seafood and produce with windows overlooking the Leipsic River. Must be 21 or older to enter.

eat.name: Fordham & Dominion Brewing Company
eat.desc: Local brewery offering tours and tastings.

eat.name: The Golden Fleece Tavern
eat.desc: The Golden Fleece Tavern is an historic bar and the site of Delaware's ratification of the Federal Constitution in 1787. Happy hour ($0.75 off all drinks) every day from 4:00-7:00, with free happy hour food on Friday. Often has a DJ or live music.

eat.name: Harvest Ridge Winery & Rebel Seed Cidery
eat.desc: Family farm winery in the serene countryside to the west of Dover, offering cidery tasting and recurring events.

see.name: Ernest Hemingway House
see.desc: Hemingway lived and wrote here for a decade. He also raised cats, the descendants of which still roam the grounds and have extra toes.

see.name: Fort Zachary Taylor
see.desc: The perfect romantic place to cuddle up with someone special, unwind, and watch the sun set as sailboats glide by... all without the crazy circus of Mallory Square. It doesn't get any more romantic in this crowded city. Nature trails, 1866 fort with a real moat, beaches, snack stand. Before Ballast Key was deeded to the US Fish and Wildlife Service in 2019, the beach area was the southernmost point in the continental US accessible to the general public, regardless of what the famous buoy at the corner of Whitehead and South Streets says.

see.name: Harry S. Truman Little White House
see.desc: A historic retreat used by President Harry S. Truman. Guided tours are available, as well as a gift shop. It's still used as a retreat and place of business by US government officials today.

see.name: Key West AIDS Memorial
see.desc: The City of Key West has lost more than a thousand of its citizens to the AIDS epidemic. Some of their names are inscribed on a memorial near the White Street Pier. The memorial is embedded in the sidewalk near the ocean, and made of flat smooth granite. The memorial was dedicated on World AIDS Day in 1997, and funded entirely through private sources. At the time of dedication, there were 730 names engraved on the memorial. There are spaces for 1,500 names, and each year more are added and dedicated in a ceremony, also on World AIDS Day in December. A group called Friends of the Key West AIDS Memorial takes care of the memorial.

see.name: Key West Art and Historical Society Museum
see.desc: Visitors can explore the preserved battlement’s collection of relics from the Civil War, learn about the wrecking and cigar-manufacturing industries which shaped the Florida Keys, view the unique folk art of Mario Sanchez and the imaginative metal sculptures of Stanley Papio, as well as meet the Ghosts of East Martello, including the infamous Robert the Doll. The building, formerly the Fort East Martello, is on the National Register of Historic Places

see.name: Key West City Cemetery
see.desc: In Key West, burial customs reflect combinations of African, Hispanic, Anglo and other mixed heritages. Due to the water table of the Keys, most burials are in above ground tombs. Grave markers with unusual inscriptions such as ''I told you I was sick'', ''Devoted Fan of Julio Iglesias'' and ''At Least I know where he's sleeping tonight'' are not unusual. Cemetery maps are available at the front gate.

see.name: Key West Lighthouse
see.desc: With a panoramic view of the island.

see.name: Shipwreck Museum
see.desc: Offers a panoramic view of the island from its observation tower.

see.name: Southernmost Point
see.desc: A "buoy" (actually an old sewer junction painted to look like a buoy) placed at this point contains an inaccurate message that it is the southernmost point in the continental USA. The true southernmost point of Florida is on Ballast Key, an island about 9 miles (14 km) from Key West, which is open to boaters during daylight hours only for minimally invasive activities such as birdwatching and nature photography. The marker is also not the southernmost point on Key West island—a private yard is immediately southeast of the buoy, and the island's true southernmost point is in the Truman Annex west of the buoy, which is U.S. Navy property and can be entered only by authorized Navy personnel. Even before Ballast Key was opened to public access, the buoy wasn't even the southernmost point that could be accessed by the public—''that'' would be the beach area of Fort Zachary Taylor (see above). Nonetheless, it's one of the city's most visited and photographed spots. Expect large crowds on the weekends, and waiting for your turn to take a picture is the norm.

see.name: Wildlife Rescue of the Florida Keys
see.desc: This rescue operation has released more than 2,000 healed animals into the wild since 1993. They take care of any animal that needs attention, from sea birds to raccoons, and at any given time you might see up to 100 creatures healing at the center. They come from all over, from the Seven Mile bridge to the Dry Tortugas. You can visit the patients any day from 9AM to 5PM, and the park is open sunup to sundown. It's free, but they like donations and volunteers.

see.name: Key West Aquarium
see.desc: Aquarium featuring a touch tank for hands-on experiences with sea anemones, plus guided tours.

see.name: Key West Nature Preserve
see.desc: Two entrances on Atlantic Blvd. Ocean front property that has been turned into an accessible natural area. Enjoy seeing local Key West wildlife such as lizards, butterflies and maybe even a snake.

see.name: Florida Keys Eco-Discovery Center
see.desc: Truman Annex Waterfront. With its touch screens, stunning photos, and roomy theater showing a short high-definition film about the Keys ecosystems, this educational center has become a hit with families. It's a fun way to learn about reef and mangrove habitats before or after an excursion. The newest addition is the Living Reef exhibit, which features a 2,500-gallon reef aquarium. Free admission and parking on-site.

see.name: Sebago Watersports
see.desc: WReef snorkeling, sunset sails, parasailing, all-day adventures from the tame ''Island Ting'' to the active ''Power Adventure''. The parasailing tends to be a bit brief (13 minutes), but the crew is friendly.

see.name: Fury Water Adventures
see.desc: It offers snorkeling, parasailing, jet skiing, kayaking, rock climbing, water trampoline, sunset sails and cruises, reef eco tours, and glass bottom boat tours. Fury also offers combo packages such as the Ultimate Adventure, the Rum & Reggae, and the Commotion on the Ocean.

see.name: Diving in Key West
see.desc: Offering daily dive trips to the reefs near Key West.

see.name: Floridays
see.desc: Luxury sailboat operating out of the Hyatt Centric Hotel offering daily snorkeling and evening Sunset Sailing adventures. A beautiful well maintained vessel taking much smaller groups that what you might find on some of the other commercial vessels in and around Key West. A very popular choice for weddings and private charters.

see.name: Astro City
see.desc: A popular stop for families on their way to and from the beach. Located directly across the street from Higgs beach.

see.name: Key West Fishing
see.desc: Offers charters, guides, and fishing information for Key West. Includes private and group fishing charters.

see.name: Sunset Celebration
see.desc: This event begins every evening a few hours before sunset and is much like a street carnival, with vendors, performers, food, and fun. Also a great photo op for some of the most beautiful sunsets.

see.name: Keywest Scavenger Hunt
see.desc: Since winning the prestigious "Venture Award" from the Key West Chamber of Commerce, The Southernmost Scavenger Hunt has expanded to offer a wider variety of custom designed features to their ever-popular scavenger hunts.

see.name: Restless Native Charters
see.desc: Luxury sailing catamaran for sail/dive, sunset sails, private partys, weddings/proposals. Upscale food and drink and a great adventure on the water.

see.name: Honest Works Island Pottery co
see.desc: Honest Works Island Pottery Co. is a vibrant art gallery and active studio space in Old town Key West. Stop on by and watch the pottery in the making or make it yourself. Honest Works offers pottery classes, as well as, paint your own pottery for locals and tourist alike. In this dynamic studio space artists, Adam Russell and Kelly Lever, create and display their own colorful island pottery. Come on in and fell the artist energy flowing!

see.name: Conch Republic Independence Celebration
see.desc: Events include a "battle" reenactment, drag race, bed race, pirate party, regatta, conch shell-blowing contest, arts and crafts fair. Republic passports available online.

see.name: Fantasy Fest
see.desc: Annual event.

see.name: Gay Spring Break
see.desc: Annual event held in February, March, and April targeting college-age LGBT students.

see.name: Womenfest
