see.name: Lake Eden Arts Festival (LEAF)
see.desc: Twice each year, multicultural music and arts non-profit event held at scenic Camp Rockmont, in nearby Black Mountain.

see.name: Asheville FringeArts Festival
see.desc: Held annually at the end of January.

see.name: Asheville Herb Festival
see.desc: The largest herb festival in Southeast, offering herb plants, herbs, books, soaps, herbal crafts, vinegars, medicinal herbs, lotions, tinctures, teas, dried flowers, herbal baked goods, and herbal gifts. Held each May.

see.name: Downtown After Five
see.desc: Held the third Friday of each month from May through September, featuring free outdoor local music and plenty of shopping and eating opportunities.

see.name: Shindig on the Green
see.desc: Music and dance traditions of Southern Appalachia. Held from the end of June through the beginning of September.

see.name: Mountain Dance and Folk Festival
see.desc: Mountain fiddlers, banjo pickers, dulcimer sweepers, and dancers. Held the first weekend in August.

see.name: Goombay! Festival
see.desc: An African-Caribbean style festival. Held each August.

see.name: Organicfest
see.desc: A festive day of live music, organic food and drink, organic and green goods, and fun activities for kids of all ages.

see.name: Great Smokies Craft Brewers Brewgrass Festival
see.desc: Over 30 American breweries showcase more than 100 different beers, along with music from national and regional bluegrass musicians. Held each September.

see.name: Moogfest
see.desc: Electronic music festival honoring the late innovator Bob Moog, inventor of the Moog synthesizer. Held on Halloween weekend.

see.name: Blue Ridge Pride
see.desc: A forum for building community and to honor the many facets of the lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender family.

see.name: Asheville Civic Center
see.desc: The arena has a capacity of 7,654.

see.name: Grey Eagle Tavern & Music Hall
see.desc: Has a capacity 550.

see.name: The Orange Peel
see.desc: Standing capacity of 942, shows local and nationally touring acts. In 2008, ''Rolling Stone'' magazine named the Peel one of the top five rock clubs in America.

see.name: The Emerald Lounge
see.desc: A hot spot for live music and dancing.

see.name: Thomas Wolfe Auditorium
see.desc: Has a capacity of 2,431.

see.name: Asheville Community Theatre
see.desc: A volunteer-driven community theatre.

see.name: Asheville Contemporary Dance Theatre
see.desc: Western North Carolina's first modern dance company. A diverse repertory reflects both traditional and experimental forms of modern dance.

see.name: Asheville Lyric Opera
see.desc: Productions of opera, operetta, and musicals, performed in the company’s home, the Diana Wortham Theatre.

see.name: Asheville Symphony
see.desc: Presents seven full orchestra concerts a year at the Thomas Wolfe Auditorium in the Asheville Civic Center.

see.name: Diane Wortham Theatre
see.desc: Located within the Pack Place Education Arts and Science Center on Pack Square, the theatre offers live performances of music, theatre and dance by nationally touring artists and professional regional arts groups.

see.name: Montford Park Players
see.desc: Free Shakespeare and other classic plays held at the Hazel Robinson Amphitheatre in Montford.

see.name: North Carolina Stage Company
see.desc: Asheville's only professional theatre. Voted Best Local Theatre by readers of Mountain Xpress for four years running. Winner George A. Parides Award for Outstanding Professional Theatre, North Carolina Theatre Conference. NC Stage Company has something either in rehearsal or performance 49 out of 52 weeks.

see.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
see.desc: Some of the most beautiful (and abundant) waterfalls can be reached via the [[Blue Ridge Parkway]]. Park your car on any Parkway overlook and there will most likely be a trail nearby. Popular spots include Mount Pisgah (15 miles south on the Parkway), Graveyard Fields (25 miles south on the Parkway), Craggy Gardens (24 miles north on the Parkway), and Mount Mitchell, the eastern United States highest mountain (35 miles/1 hour drive north on the Parkway). The Parkway intersects Asheville at US 25, US 70, US 74A & NC 191.

see.name: Botanical Gardens at Asheville
see.desc: A half-mile loop across streams, through meadows, and over a woodland ridge to a wildflower cove with an authentic log cabin. Just three miles north of downtown beside the University of North Carolina at Asheville.

see.name: North Carolina Arboretum
see.desc: A 434-acre facility with a Visitor Education Center, state-of-the-art greenhouses, beautiful gardens, and walking trails.

see.name: Pisgah National Forest
see.desc: Much of Western North Carolina is covered by national forest, making it a hiker’s paradise. For maps or information on great places to hike, call the National Forest Service.

see.name: Lutheridge
see.desc: Faith-based outdoor camp and conference center located between Asheville and Hendersonville. Lutheridge offers a variety of summer programs for elementary to high school aged youth and hosts retreats and conferences from fall to spring. Lutheridge is affiliated with the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America.

see.name: Climbmax
see.desc: An indoor rock climbing gym in downtown Asheville.

see.name: Biltmore Estate Carriage & Trail Ride Barns
see.desc: Lessons, guided trail rides, shows, clinics, and camps. Must pay entrance fee to Biltmore estate.

see.name: Food Lion Skate Park
see.desc: An outdoor skateboarding park in downtown Asheville.

see.name: The Asheville Tourists
see.desc: Come support Asheville's own minor league baseball team! The Tourists offer a full season running from May through early September, and every Thursday is 'Thirsty Thursday' where a cup of draft beer is only $1.

see.name: The Asheville Grizzlies
see.desc: A professional minor league men's football team.

see.name: The Blue Ridge Rollergirls
see.desc: Women's flat-track roller derby league.

see.name: Asheville Community Yoga
see.desc: All sorts of yoga by various local teachers.

see.name: Asheville Yoga Center
see.desc: Offering all styles of Hatha yoga.

eat.name: Heiwa Shokudo
eat.desc: Traditional Japanese and sushi.

eat.name: Mela
eat.desc: Authentic Indian food in a beautiful and exotic atmosphere. Full bar available.

eat.name: Wasabi
eat.desc: Japanese restaurant and sushi bar.

eat.name: The Market Place
eat.desc: Innovative "farm to table" cuisine.

eat.name: Table
eat.desc: New-American cuisine with a daily written menu.

eat.name: Limones
eat.desc: Upscale fresh Mexican-Californian cuisine. Reservations recommended.

eat.name: Mamacitas
eat.desc: Fresh, made from scratch Mexican cuisine.

eat.name: Salsa
eat.desc: Mexican-Caribbean food.

eat.name: Bouchon
eat.desc: French comfort food of the Lyon area of France and wine bar.

eat.name: Cucina 24
eat.desc: Traditional Italian. Reservations recommended.

eat.name: Zambra
eat.desc: Tapas and Spanish cuisine in a very romantic atmosphere.

eat.name: Early Girl Eatery
eat.desc: Made-from-scratch Southern regional cuisine using local organic produce and free-range meats.

eat.name: Tupelo Honey Cafe
eat.desc: Check this out for some delicious New Southern cuisine.

eat.name: Chop House
eat.desc: Signature steakhouse.

eat.name: Laughing Seed
eat.desc: A vegetarian/vegan restaurant with a variety of international-inspired unique dishes. Jungle-themed elegant indoor dining or great outdoor dining on Wall Street, the heart of downtown. The bar Jack of the Wood is downstairs.

eat.name: Rosetta's Kitchen
eat.desc: Vegetarian/vegan (mostly organic) food in a very unique atmosphere. It's open until 3AM on most nights, and you're sure to find an assortment of interesting characters no matter the time of day.

eat.name: Asheville Pizza and Brewing Company
eat.desc: Known to locals as the APBC or Brew n' View, is a good place to relax with a beer, pizza (available by the slice), and watch a movie for $3.

eat.name: 828 Family Pizzeria
eat.desc: New York style pizza.

eat.name: The Hop
eat.desc: Serves acclaimed ice cream (vegan selections available) made on-site.

eat.name: The Admiral
eat.desc: Menu changes daily.

eat.name: Sunny Point Cafe & Bakery
eat.desc: A great brunch spot.

eat.name: Rocky's Hot Chicken Shack
eat.desc: Delicious fried chicken as hot as you want it.

eat.name: Firestorm Cafe
eat.desc: Employee-owned cafe with all vegan menu offering wraps, handmade pastries, and more exotic options. Unusual selection of progressive books, anarchist pamphlets, and free internet. Firestorms hosts community events and concerts on a regular basis.

eat.name: Fig
eat.desc: Reservations recommended.

eat.name: Asheville Brewing Company
eat.desc: A brewpub with their own locally-brewed beers on tap and a full liquor bar, piles of board games, and a large outdoor covered patio with giant movie screen.

eat.name: Barley's Taproom
eat.desc: A popular destination with an expansive variety of beers, local, regional, and continental. 52 beers on tap. Small stage with live music 3-4 nights a week, no cover charge. Upstairs Billiard Room with four tables available by the hour.

eat.name: Bier Garden
eat.desc: Over 200 beers from around the world and a full liquor bar. For the sports fans, they have 16 televisions including a 15-foot screen.

eat.name: Jack of the Wood
eat.desc: Serves its own locally-brewed Green Man Ales on tap and a limited selection of bottled beers.

eat.name: Scandals
eat.desc: A huge gay-oriented nightclub with 3 dance floors and 4 bars.

eat.name: Thirsty Monk
eat.desc: Pub specializing in Belgian beers.

eat.name: Yacht Club
eat.desc: Tiki bar/restaurant serving lunch, dinner and a late night menu. Check out their specialty cocktails, particularly the 'Pain Killer', it's served on fire.

eat.name: Asheville Pizza and Brewing Company
eat.desc: Locally brewed beer at $3.75 a pint.

eat.name: French Broad Brewery Tasting Room
eat.desc: Offers tastings, tours and live music five nights a week in a relaxed, intimate setting.

eat.name: Root Bar
eat.desc: Home of the original sport of rootball (a cross between horseshoes and bocce)! Beer only.

eat.name: Westville Pub
eat.desc: Family-oriented bar with pub grub and live music.

see.name: Bodie Island Lighthouse
see.desc: The current Bodie Island Lighthouse (pronounced “body island”) is the third that has stood in this vicinity of Bodie Island on the Outer Banks and was built in 1872. It stands {{ft

see.name: Bellamy Mansion Museum
see.desc: Tours on the hour Tu-Sa 10AM-5PM and Sunday 1-5PM. Built for planter Dr. John D. Bellamy in 1859, the Bellamy Mansion is Wilmington's most spectacular example of antebellum architecture. Today, the mansion operates as a museum of history and design arts, and is owned by Preservation North Carolina. See exhibits on architectural history, historic preservation and design arts, and see the newly restored carriage house and gardens. Plans are being made for restoring the slave quarters. Free parking lot on Market St. side of the museum and free street parking on block surrounding the museum.

see.name: Burgwin-Wright Museum and Gardens
see.desc: Tours on the hour M-F with the last tour at 3:30PM. On Saturdays, tours on the half-hour, with the last tour at 3:30PM. From the house museum's own website: "Using the old jail as the foundation, the Burgwin-Wright House was built in 1770 by John Burgwin, planter, merchant, and treasurer of the colony of Carolina. In 1781, 'the most considerable house in town' was occupied by Lord Cornwallis as his headquarters shortly before his defeat and surrender at Yorktown, Virginia."

see.name: Cape Fear Museum of History and Science
see.desc: The Cape Fear Museum of History and Science collects, preserves, and interprets objects relating to the history, science and cultures of the Lower Cape Fear.

see.name: EUE / Screen Gems Studio
see.desc: Tours are offered at noon on Saturdays from September to May and Saturdays and Sundays noon and 2PM from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Tour of EUE Screen Gems Studios North Carolina takes visitors through North Carolina's film history. This one-hour walking tour includes visits to the sets of Dawson’s Creek, Iron Man 3 and One Tree Hill.

see.name: Battleship North Carolina
see.desc: Moored across the river from downtown Wilmington, this battleship offers visitors the chance to envision the daily life and fierce combat her crew faced in the Pacific Theatre during World War II. Exhibits tell the story of the ship's crew through their oral histories, photographs, and mementos. The tour is self-guided and is well-marked so that you can tour at your own pace. Allow at least two hours for the tour, but for the true enthusiast, you can spend much more than that.

see.name: Stanley Rehder Carnivorous Plant Garden
see.desc: See carnivorous plants including Venus flytraps.

see.name: Wilmington Railroad Museum
see.desc: Has a great collection of displays that are fun and educational.

see.name: Cameron Art Museum
see.desc: Art museum with changing exhibitions and different art programs and lectures.

see.name: Museum of the Bizarre
see.desc: Children-friendly museum with unusual art and science installations and items.

see.name: Jungle Rapids
see.desc: Water park closed during off season but dry park open all year round. Hours vary and park may close due to inclement weather, so call ahead. Its main feature is the water park, but it includes an arcade, mini golf and go karts. Prices vary for admittance to the waterpark, but the best price is the 4PM-7PM $14.95 for all ages special.

see.name: Airlie Gardens
see.desc: Airlie Gardens encompasses 67 acres of quintessential Southern gardens with 10 acres of freshwater lakes. Features include azaleas, camellias, statuary and the Historic Airlie Oak. This once privately owned garden was purchased for the public by New Hanover County in January, 1999.

see.name: Watersmyth Kayaking
see.desc: Kayaking tours and lessons.

see.name: Tour Old Wilmington
see.desc: Tour Old Wilmington and discover hidden history and a lost time as we travel to Wilmington during the Victorian Era (1837- 1901) Learn about Wilmington’s rich and colorful history as we reveal what life was like in Wilmington during the Civil War, customs and traditions of the day, sea tales, and folklore. Call for tour times. Walking tours start at the foot of Market and Water Streets, be sure to look for the Victorian Lady!

see.name: Ghost Walk of Old Wilmington
see.desc: Riverfront at Market & Water Streets.

see.name: Haunted Cotton Exchange
see.desc: Scary, creepy and mostly ghostly tales. Chills and thrills await you at one of the most historic and haunted locations in Wilmington. Bring your camera.

see.name: North Carolina Azalea Festival
see.desc: A week-long festival held every April, with music, events, exhibits, tours, community pride, and the beautiful flowers in bloom.

eat.name: Flaming Amy's Burrito Barn
eat.desc: Mainly serves burritos and other Mexican style food. Advertises its food as "hot, fast, cheap and easy" and is a local favorite. Restaurant features a psychedelic theme. They have a restaurant on Carolina Beach also.

eat.name: Plaza Mariachi
eat.desc: Traditional Mexican. Great food, chips and drinks make it a local favorite.

eat.name: The Bento Box
eat.desc: Delicious sushi, fresh ingredients all at reasonable price and incredible atmosphere.

eat.name: Blueberry's Grill Wilmington
eat.desc: Grill restaurant that serves [https://blueberrysgrill.com/wilmington/menu-breakfast.html breakfast] and [https://blueberrysgrill.com/wilmington/menu-lunch.html lunch], as well as [https://blueberrysgrill.com/wilmington/menu-cocktails.html brunch cocktails].

eat.name: Dockside Restaurant & Marina
eat.desc: Open daily 11AM-until. On the water just south of the Wrightsville Beach drawbridge. Locals' favorite "place to be" for friendly Carolina service, relaxed island lifestyle. Fresh seafood, famous drinks, families love kid's menu. Live music most weekends.

eat.name: Fat Tony's Italian Pub
eat.desc: Combine homemade Italian food and 24 draft beers and you've got the country's latest concept: an Italian pub!

eat.name: Szechuan 132
eat.desc: High-quality Chinese restaurant offering American-Chinese mainstays as well as authentic Asian dishes.

eat.name: Circa 1922
eat.desc: Affordable tapas and fine dining with a wonderful wine selection and terrific ambience, located in the Front Street riverfront nightlife area.

eat.name: Elijah's
eat.desc: Main dining room closed daily from 3PM-5PM, oyster bar open all day, reservations are recommended. Casual American Grill and oyster bar, downtown on the river. Sunset hues are said to be spectacular.

eat.name: Hiro Japanese Steak and Seafood House
eat.desc: Lunch on Sundays 11AM-4PM. Japanese cuisine. Includes sushi bar and sashimi. Chefs prepare your meal right at your table.

eat.name: Hell's Kitchen
eat.desc: Formerly a set for the TV show ''Dawson's Creek'', which was filmed locally, Hell's Kitchen is a popular downtown destination for good times among friends. A pub-style setting and a menu of pub sandwiches, burritos and nachos. Full liquor bar available and offers a wide variety of draught and microbrew beers. Well known Wilmington nightclub "Rum Runners" merged with this establishment, bringing their signature dueling pianos show with them.

eat.name: Haunted Pub Crawl
eat.desc: Pub crawl where you get to hear stories about dark events in the city's past.

eat.name: Front Street Brewery
eat.desc: A great brewpub in the historic downtown district of Wilmington featuring great beer and good food. Prices are good, and they have daily $1.99 mug special of one of their delicious house beers, as well as cheap lunch specials. Live entertainment on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights.

eat.name: Cape Fear Wine and Beer
eat.desc: A hybrid specialty beer and wine shop/old-world public house, CFWB offers the most impressive selection of microbrews, imports, and wines in eastern NC. 12 beers (and a mead!) rotate on their various taps and draught engines and they boast a selection of over 300 beers and 200 wines. The theme is best described as German beer hall and UK pub have a weird three-way with a bunch of vikings while listening to gnarly punk music. The staff is exceptionally knowledgeable and helpful, and it is an off-premises store.

eat.name: Wilmington Brewing Company
eat.desc: A 11,800-sq ft facility that includes a 3-barrel brewery, tasting room, and a Homebrew supply store offering fresh local beer straight from the tank.

see.name: Roger Maris Museum
see.desc: Museum of the baseball player Roger Maris, who went to high school in Fargo and went on to play for the New York Yankees.

see.name: North Dakota State University
see.desc: A nice campus to walk around and see Midwest college life in all its glory. They also have tours. It's a decent size campus with lots to see like the Memorial garden and the creek.

see.name: Germans from Russia Heritage Collection
see.desc: A collection of various photographs and artifacts from Germans from Russia who immigrated to the surrounding area. Hosts various exhibits from within the NDSU library building.

see.name: Plains Art Museum
see.desc: Surprisingly interesting contemporary art museum.

see.name: Fargo Air Museum
see.desc: Museum focused on aviation history and machinery. Closed on all major holidays such as Easter, July 4, Christmas Eve and Day, and New Year's Day. Some days may be booked for private events, so check the website.

see.name: Red River Zoo
see.desc: Open daily May to October, weekends only rest of year. Has red pandas.

see.name: Celebrity Walk of Fame
see.desc: The walk where more than 100 celebrities have left their marks in cement. Stars from music, the arts, politics, and sports, like: Garth Brooks, Neil Diamond, KISS, Maury Wills, Debbie Reynolds, and Governor Jesse Ventura, have left their signatures, handprints and footprints.

see.name: Downtown Murals
see.desc: Downtown is decorated with over 20 street art murals. Many of them are "interactive", for you to photograph yourself as part of the art.

see.name: Horse Racing
see.desc: Season is from early August to mid-September.

see.name: Thunder Road Family Fun Park
see.desc: Go-kart racing, bumper cars, laser tag, batting cages, mini golf, and an arcade. Open May–September. Inside usually opens in April.

see.name: Bill's Gun Shop & Range
see.desc: Indoor gun range with a huge variety of firearms available to rent for target shooting. The staff is friendly, helpful, and happy to teach beginners, so even if you've never touched a gun before, you'll be welcomed. High-quality eye and ear protection is essential and available for sale. Closed-toe, closed-heel shoes are required. Make sure to fill out the online waiver on their website, and be prepared to give them your ID to hold on to while you're on the range.

see.name: Suite Shots
see.desc: A large golf driving range. Many lanes and indoor simulators. Clubs can be rented or you can bring your own. They have left handed and right handed clubs. Also serves food.

see.name: Fargo Billiards and Gastropub
see.desc: Pool hall in southern Fargo, also serves bar food. There are 56 tables. Also has trivia nights.

see.name: Kingpinz Social
see.desc: Bowling alley, arcade, laser tag, and escape rooms. They also host events and have a restaurant.

see.name: Fargo Kids Play Museum
see.desc: Children's museum and play area with stations. Also has childcare.

see.name: Fargodome
see.desc: Offers athletic events (most notably North Dakota State football games), broadway shows, music concerts. During some concerts 1/4 of the population fits inside the Fargodome.

see.name: Fargo Theatre
see.desc: The Fargo Theater show mostly independent films, on actual film, not digital. Inside the theatre there is a statue of Marge Olmstead Gunderson, of the movie ''Fargo'' carved out of wood. Inside on the stage is a functional Wurlitzer pipe organ that is occasionally used to score silent films.

see.name: The Aquarium
see.desc: Concert venue usually hosting metal or punk shows. Caters to local bands, too.

see.name: Fargo-Moorhead Redhawks
see.desc: Minor league baseball. While you are there, check out the Maury Wills Museum.

see.name: North Dakota State Bison
see.desc: The university's sports teams, competing in eight men's and eight women's sports, mostly in the Summit League. The most prominent program by far is the football team, a major power at the Division I FCS (second) level, including nine national championships in 11 seasons (2011–2015, 2017–2019, 2021) and the most recent title in 2024. With the Summit League not sponsoring football, NDSU plays that sport in the Missouri Valley Football Conference. Most Bison teams play on campus, including the football team (the Fargodome is owned by the city, but the underlying land is owned by the university and part of the campus). Football games frequently sell out, but tickets for other sports are easier to find. Tip to fit in with the locals: the "S" in "Bison" is locally pronounced with a "z" sound instead of the "s" sound found in most other American English dialects.

see.name: Vietnam Week
see.desc: Dedicated to Vietnam era.

see.name: Fargo Marathon
see.desc: Usually in May.

eat.name: Grand Junction
eat.desc: East Coast Style Subs serves hot subs grilled fresh right in front of you. A local favorite. Try the Chicken Cordon Bleu sandwich, very delicious.

eat.name: Boppa's Bagels
eat.desc: Boppa's Bagels makes wonderful bagels, of note are their speciality bagels, that are also available at some coffee shops around the city.

eat.name: Brewhalla
eat.desc: Indoor market with several food stalls. Also has an attached hotel.

eat.name: Los Vaqueros Taqueria
eat.desc: Mexican restaurant offering authentic dishes and drinks. Friendly staff and nice decor inside.

eat.name: Labby's Grill and Bar
eat.desc: Grill and bar featuring sandwiches, hamburgers, and more. Good atmosphere.

eat.name: Kroll's Diner
eat.desc: German and American 1950s diner. Also has locations in other North Dakota cities.

eat.name: The Bison Turf
eat.desc: Bar and grill right by the NDSU campus. Popular with students. Features a pool table, darts, a second floor bar, and a rooftop lounge.

eat.name: Herd and Horns
eat.desc: Restaurant and bar popular with students at NDSU. Has hamburgers, sandwiches, salads, etc.

eat.name: Pho Thien Kim & Boba
eat.desc: Vietnamese restaurant south of the NDSU campus. Serves pho, bubble tea, sub sandwiches, as well as rice with grilled meats.

eat.name: Passage to India
eat.desc: An excellent Indian buffet place. A flavourful and delightful selection from soup to dessert is available.

eat.name: Himalayan Yak
eat.desc: Offers excellent Nepalese and Indian food. Lunch buffet offered M - Su at 11AM - 2:30PM

eat.name: Würst Bier Hall
eat.desc: German-style restaurant and bar. Extensive list of local and exotic sausages (including two that are vegetarian and vegan), soft pretzels, and a variety of other German dishes. The drink menu has lots of beers and a few cocktails. Also has a location in [[West Fargo]].

eat.name: Frank's Lounge
eat.desc: Home of the Pink Pussycat, this "lounge" has a good atmosphere that resembles a sports bar. Serves food and alcohol and kids sometimes permitted. Also sells merchandise.

eat.name: 701 Eateries (Prairie Kitchen & Camp Lonetree)
eat.desc: Contains two restaurants in the same building: Prairie Kitchen is the main interior restaurant area, and Camp Lonetree is a bar and grill, upstairs. They also operate a rooftop patio year round. This is all housed in the old Acme Dairy building. They serve modern American food.

eat.name: Mezzaluna & The Drawing Room
eat.desc: Fine dining in downtown Fargo in a very unassuming location.

eat.name: Porter Creek Hardwood Grill
eat.desc: Modern American restaurant with on display grilling. Features a large menu with many options for grilled food, salads, and more.

eat.name: Bismarck Tavern
eat.desc: The PBR is always cold, all the whiskey drinks are doubles, and pull tabs litter the dirty floor. This downtown Fargo watering hole is Fargo's best dive bar. Black jack tables, off-sale liquor, pool, and pinball are available. Also the oldest bar in Fargo.

eat.name: Dempsey's Public House
eat.desc: Irish pub. Free popcorn, karaoke, and a side room with various amenities. LGBTQ+ friendly bar!

eat.name: Blarney Irish Pub
eat.desc: Irish pub featuring pub food as well as beers and ales on tap.

eat.name: Rooters Bar
eat.desc: Bar made up of two different buildings with the center wall removed, and bars on each side. It has darts, pool, and a blackjack table. Mostly serves drinks and the only food is microwaved pizza. There are specialty drinks like their root beer and green lantern.

eat.name: Fort Noks Bar of Gold
eat.desc: Sports type bar with daily specials varying. Lots of tables as well as a blackjack table. Has daily specials. In the warmer months, the empty lot next door hosts picnic tables where people crowd and drink.

eat.name: Empire Liquors
eat.desc: Despite its name, the Empire is also a dive bar. The door on the left is the liquor store and the door on the right is the bar.

eat.name: Cowboy Jacks
eat.desc: Bar with two floors, including a rooftop lounge. Usually has a live DJ and has a long bar with lots of tables.

eat.name: Sports Bar
eat.desc: This bar is a narrow and well lit bar on the south side of downtown. Happy hour M-F 4:30-6:30PM with a dice roll dictating your options.

eat.name: Chub's Pub
eat.desc: Dive bar with nightly specials. Has a pool table, darts, slots, breathalyzer, and more. Quiet atmosphere and popular with students depending on the night. Also sells off-sale alcohol.

eat.name: The Old Broadway
eat.desc: Restaurant and bar. Art deco interior with $2 drinks before 10 PM. People tend to leave after then. Attracts lots of students. The restaurant closes at 3 PM and the bar opens at 7 PM.

eat.name: Rick's Bar
eat.desc: Bar on main avenue, also has a lounge and off-sale. Featuring live music and serves food, including a daily lunch special.

eat.name: Speck's Bar
eat.desc: Rough-around-the-edges dive bar. Pool tables and cold drinks, this place has seen a lot.

eat.name: Duffy's Tavern
eat.desc: Little bar with a cast of regulars. Relaxing atmosphere, and has a happy hour on weekdays. Does not serve food. Cash only.

eat.name: Wild Terra
eat.desc: A cider and wine bar! Relaxed and family friendly atmosphere, and it has a happy hour on weekdays.

eat.name: Babb's Coffee House
eat.desc: A fantastic independent coffee shop located across the street from the Fargo Theater downtown. Also serves breakfast and lunch with vegan options. Credit cards are accepted for a $0.25 surcharge.

eat.name: Atomic Coffee
eat.desc: Coffee shop with a lot of atmosphere and a varied seating selection.

see.name: North Dakota State Capitol Building
see.desc: The state's tallest building, and the location of all three branches of state government. Tours available M - F 9AM-11AM and 1-3PM year round, M - F 8AM-11AM and 1-4PM, Sa 9AM-11AM and 1-3PM, Su 1-4PM from Memorial Day to Labor Day.

see.name: Bismarck Art and Galleries Association
see.desc: Art, photography and sculptures exhibits by local, regional and national artists. Open year round, Tuesday-Friday 10AM-5PM; Saturday 1-3PM Free admission.

see.name: Buckstop Junction Missouri Valley Fairgrounds
see.desc: Reconstructed village with buildings from the late 1800s to the early 1930s. Turn-of-the-century atmosphere. By appointment. Admission fee is $2.

see.name: Camp Hancock
see.desc: State historic site. Open May 16 to September 15, W-Su 1-5PM. It was established in 1872 as a military post, Camp Creeley, then renamed Camp Hancock in 1973. Its mission was to provide protection for work gangs building the Northern Pacific Railroad. The camp headquarters, a log building, is still standing on the site.

see.name: Chief Looking's Village
see.desc: Native American village site with self-guided tour of the grounds, contains earthlodge depressions and a fortification ditch.

see.name: Dakota Zoo
see.desc: Variety of animal exhibits, including endangered monkeys, moose, and brown bears, some in natural habitats. Open late April to end of September from 10AM-8PM daily. In the winter (October to late April), open Friday to Sunday, 1-5PM. Admission for children under age two is free, $4.25 for children 2-12, $7.25 for ages 13-60, and $6.25 for 60+.

see.name: Double Ditch Indian Village
see.desc: Remains of a large Mandan Indian earthlodge village that is believed to have been inhabited for almost 300 years until 1781. Eight interactive signs provide information on the site.

see.name: Old Governor's Mansion
see.desc: State historic site. Restored Victorian mansion and carriage house. It was built in 1884, and housed 21 ND governors from 1893 to 1960. Exhibits explain the restoration process, architectural style changes, and furniture used by several governors. Open May 16 to September 15, Wednesday thru Sunday, from 1-5PM.

see.name: North Dakota Heritage Center and State Museum
see.desc: This is North Dakota's largest museum. It displays a collection of Plains Indian artifacts, and exhibits of North Dakota's military, agricultural, and natural history. Includes a special children's historical area. Sakakawea was the guide for the Lewis and Clark expedition of 1804-1806. Her statue is displayed near the center's entrance.

see.name: Theodore Roosevelt Rough Rider Hall of Fame
see.desc: In the State Capitol. Displays portraits of recipients of the Theodore Roosevelt Rough Rider Award, the state's highest, given to North Dakotans who have brought honor to the state. Open year-round, Monday-Friday 8AM-5PM and during Memorial Day to Labor day, also open on Saturday 9AM-4PM and on Sunday 1-4PM.

see.name: Lewis and Clark Riverboat
see.desc: A 150-passenger paddle wheel riverboat based at the Port of Bismarck, River Road, Bismarck. Afternoon and evening round-trip cruises on the Missouri River from the historic Port of Bismarck to Fort Lincoln and the On-A-Slant Mandan Village. Dinner and beverage service available for regular cruises and charters. Narrations and reenactments provided during cruises. Call for regular scheduled cruises from April through October.

see.name: Huff Hills Ski Area
see.desc: Located in the buttes on the western banks of the Missouri River, is the largest downhill ski area in North Dakota, with a vertical drop of 450 feet (140 m). Huff Hills is 18 miles (29 km) south of Mandan on ND State Highway 1806. The scenic drive takes around 45 minutes from Bismarck, and around 30 minutes from Mandan.

see.name: Grand 22 Theater
see.desc: Locally-owned. The favorite among local movie enthusiasts. It offers stadium seating in most of its theaters. The theater features curved screens, two giant screens, rocking seats, a theater with many loveseats, and lavish decor.

see.name: Hockey
see.desc: The Bismarck Bobcats are a local NAHL hockey team that plays most weekends between October and April in the VFW All-Seasons Arena.

see.name: Bismarck Event Center
see.desc: Offers the occasional concert, featuring performers such as Clay Aiken.

see.name: Superslide Amusement Park
see.desc: Superslide, Ferris wheel, carousel, batting cages, tubs, swings, bumper cars, critter track, whisper carts, mini-golf, bankshot basketball. Open from May through mid-September, weather permitting, daily from noon to 10PM.

see.name: Dakota OutRight
see.desc: A non-profit organization that serves as a regional community resource and provides gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) diversity education and promotes unity within the LGBT community and allies in western and central North Dakota.

eat.name: Kroll's Diner
eat.desc: American and German cuisine. Famous for their Knoephla soup, which you can purchase by the bucket.

eat.name: Scotty's Drive-In
eat.desc: A locally owned, retro-style drive-in from 1965. One of the oldest restaurants in the city. Burgers, hot dogs, fries – all the things you'd expect, plus the possibility of a dill pickle milkshake at the end.

eat.name: The Walrus
eat.desc: A local favorite, The Walrus has been open since 1996. Try any one of their signature pasta dishes, unique pizzas, house-made soups, or select from 41 beers on tap, in addition to their reasonably sized wine menu. Live music on Tuesdays.

eat.name: Fireflour Pizza
eat.desc: Hand made pizzas fire roasted in a stone oven. Free parking up to 2 hours with $10 purchase.

eat.name: Space Aliens Grill & Bar
eat.desc: BBQ and pizza, in an alien themed atmosphere. Contains an arcade for the young, and young at heart.

eat.name: Peacock Alley American Grill and Bar
eat.desc: In the historic Patterson Hotel Building, within walking distance of the Bismarck Civic Center and Bismarck's downtown events. A healthy fresh lunch menu is available daily. Voted the best martini year after year and featuring 23 different tap beers.

eat.name: Bistro
eat.desc: Consistently rated best restaurant in Bismarck by readers of the Bismarck Tribune. It features a variety of dishes including regional Italian specialties. Thursday night is sushi night with live music.

eat.name: 40 Steak and Seafood
eat.desc: Another well-known fine-dining establishment in Bismarck. Monday night is sushi night with live music.

eat.name: Pirogue Grille
eat.desc: The restaurant concept features Midwest regional cuisine that changes with the seasons. Featured menu items include walleye, bison, duck, and house-made venison sausage. Great selection of desserts and breads, all made in house; extensive wine list featuring many different varietals.

eat.name: Kobe's Japanese Steakhouse and Sushi Bar
eat.desc: Come for the sushi, stay for the Teppanyaki grill show. A variety of sake, beer, wine, and spirits are also available.

eat.name: Steep Me
eat.desc: A tea shop that is a daily stop for locals. Once a dream by a local tea-maker is now a bustling business.

see.name: Medora Musical
see.desc: Good if you like bards who can weave an intricate story of the Old West and lots of cowboys prancing around.

see.name: Minot Railroad Museum
see.desc: The museum has provided its guests with a glimpse at the fascinating history of the westward railroad expansion since its opening in 1986.

see.name: Riverwalk of Minot
see.desc: A 2.5-mile (4 km) walking and biking trail along the Souris River, which is accessible from a number of Minot attractions including the '''Railroad Museum''' and '''Roosevelt Park'''.

see.name: Roosevelt Park and Zoo
see.desc: Roosevelt Park is the city's largest park. Features include a zoo, a swimming pool, and a 2/5ths scale railroad you can take a ride on around the park, in addition to gardens, walking paths, picnic shelters, tennis courts, and a band shell. Be sure to check out the sundial near the train station and the statue of Theodore Roosevelt in the southwest part of the park.

see.name: Scandinavian Heritage Park
see.desc: A 14-acre (6 hectares) park highlighting the Scandinavian roots of the region. Feature of the park include a 230-year-old house from Norway and a stave church.

see.name: Dakota Territory Air Museum
see.desc: More than 60 airplanes on display, both military and civilian ones from both world wars to the modern day. The collections include a large number of airworthy WWII airplanes.

see.name: Lillian and Coleman Taube Museum of Art
see.desc: This venue has over 1600 square feet (150 m2) of gallery space, for emerging and established talent locally, regionally, and internationally. Showcase guest artists and member’s work, as well as maintaining a permanent collection. The gallery's Museum Gift Shop sells ND artists' work. Tours are welcome anytime.

see.name: St. Leo the Great Catholic Church
see.desc: Red brick church with two towers, sticking out among the otherwise mostly box-shaped buildings of the town.

see.name: The North Dakota State Fair
see.desc: The North Dakota [[State Fair]] is one of the biggest entertainment events of the year, bringing big name concerts, carnival rides, and fairway fare. The fair runs 9 days, from the second-to-last Friday in July to the last Saturday in July.

see.name: Norsk Høstfest
see.desc: The Norsk Høstfest (Norwegian autumn festival) is North America's largest Scandinavian heritage festival, running more than 25 years. The Høstfest, like the State Fair, brings in big-name entertainers to Minot, along with a lot of other folks! The Norsk Høstfest runs 4 days, in late September or early October. See [[Nordic migration to North America]] for context.

eat.name: Charlie's Main Street Cafe
eat.desc: American fare. Open for breakfast and lunch.

eat.name: Homesteader's Restaurant
eat.desc: Downhome cooking.

eat.name: China Star
eat.desc: Chinese buffet and Mongolian barbecue. Open lunch and dinner. Local delivery.

eat.name: Planet Pizza
eat.desc: Pizza and video games! The place to take your children. Party room available. Local delivery.

eat.name: Sammy's Pizza
eat.desc: Italian cuisine. Local delivery.

eat.name: Primo
eat.desc: Italian and American cuisine. Biggest list of wines, scotches, and cognacs in town. If there is a place to wine and dine in Minot, this is it. Open 24 hours. Private rooms available. This restaurant does not take reservations.

eat.name: The Blue Rider
eat.desc: Dive bar, in business since 1994. 16 beers on tap, a selection of cocktails and snacks. Sometimes live music, Trivia night on Wednesdays, free nachos on Thursdays.

eat.name: Sports on Tap
eat.desc: Sports bar.

see.name: Goodtime III
see.desc: See Cleveland by water via Lake Erie and/or the Cuyahoga River. Dining and entertainment available.

see.name: Lady Caroline
see.desc: Lakefront and river dining cruises departing from the west bank of the Flats.

see.name: African American Heritage Trail
see.desc: This tour provides a perspective of the experience and impact of Cleveland's African American community.

eat.name: Great Lakes Brewing Company
eat.desc: The restaurant is in the Ohio City district of Cleveland. The microbrews are available at many bars, restaurants, grocery stores, and even gas stations. The restaurant has gunshots in its walls from Eliot Ness, the former Cleveland Chief of Police, and the FBI man who busted the mob in the early 20th century.

see.name: Creek Council Oak Tree
see.desc: It was under the Creek Council Oak Tree in 1836 that the Lochapoka Creek Indians kindled a ceremonial fire using live coals they had carried from their Alabama homeland. This oak was Tulsa's first town hall, first conference room, first church and first court of law. This tree symbolizes the spirit of Tulsa's early settlers.

see.name: Penguins on Parade
see.desc: There are dozens of {{ft

see.name: Greenwood Cultural Center
see.desc: Serves to promote the history of Tulsa's Greenwood District, which was home to one of the worst racially-motivated massacres in American history (in 1921). Special performances are often held at this center.

see.name: Gilcrease Museum
see.desc: Touted as the "Museum of The Americas", has one of the world's largest collections of Western and Native American art and artifacts and constantly changing exhibits on a yearly basis. The gift shop has a good collection of art, jewelry, music and books as well. A must-see attraction for any visit to Tulsa.

see.name: Oklahoma Jazz Hall of Fame
see.desc: Housed in the beautiful Art Deco-style Union Station Depot, many local jazz performances are held here.

see.name: The Philbrook Museum of Art
see.desc: In a former residence of local oilman Waite Phillips, has changing exhibits, a sculpture garden, art and artifacts from around the World, and a gift shop unlike anything else in Tulsa.

see.name: Sherwin Miller Museum of Jewish Art
see.desc: The largest collection of Judaica in the American Southwest, flagship of The Fenster/Sanditen Cultural Center. As an arts education institution, and the only American Jewish museum in the region, utilizes both art and history to preserve and present Jewish culture.

see.name: Tulsa Air and Space Museum
see.desc: TASM collection highlights include a [[WWII]] German jet engine, an F-14 Tomcat, two of Burt Rutan's experimental aircraft, a locally-built gyrocopter by Spartan Aeronautics, and Art-Deco sections of the original Tulsa International Airport Terminal. TASM also has many historical and interactive exhibits of interest to young and old alike.

see.name: BOK Center
see.desc: Tulsa's sleek, and modern center is the pride of the city. Opened in 2008, it has hosted such acts as The Eagles, Celine Dion, Elton John, and Billy Joel. With fine dining nearby and numerous hotels to stay at, this center is the centerpiece of Vision 2025, a plan to revitalize Downtown and certain parts of the city.

see.name: The Center of the Universe
see.desc: At the top of a pedestrian bridge in Tulsa. The bridge goes over the railroad tracks from Archer St. to First St. West of the Jazz Depot and immediately north of the Williams Center Tower. If you stand on the opposite side of the brick circle from someone else, you hear their echo, but not your own. If you stand at the center of the brick circle and talk, you will hear yourself echo, but others will not hear any echo. Overlooking the Center of the Universe area is a large, totem-like steel sculpture called Artificial Cloud.

see.name: The Expo Building
see.desc: Contains what was once the largest unobstructed indoor area in the world. The "Golden Driller" in front is still pretty impressive. Hosts numerous shows including home and garden shows, arts & crafts events, boat show, gun and knife shows.

see.name: The Performing Arts Center
see.desc: Downtown, the "PAC" (pronounced pee-ay-see) shows the annual presentation of ''The Nutcracker'', in addition to various operatic, musical, and dramatic shows throughout the year. Tickets and scheduling available online.

see.name: River Parks
see.desc: There is a lovely cafe down around 21st and they have live music from time to time when it is warm out. There is a new complex, Riverwalk Crossing at 101st in Riverside. It has a movie theatre and many restaurants, with a wonderful atmosphere.

see.name: Route 66
see.desc: The University of Tulsa is located nearby, and Tulsa Promenade mall is {{mi

see.name: The Spotlight Theater
see.desc: On Riverside Drive between 15th and 21st, it has shows every Saturday night of "The Drunkard"-America's longest running show-followed by "Olio", an old-fashioned vaudeville affair. Family friendly and very fun, The Drunkard is a must for any Tulsa visit!

see.name: The Gathering Place
see.desc: A huge park with a lot of attractions.

see.name: Tulsa Drillers
see.desc: Catch a [[baseball]] game with the Tulsa Drillers. The Drillers, a AA minor league team associated with the Colorado Rockies, play in ONEOK Field, in the Greenwood neighborhood.

see.name: Tulsa Zoo
see.desc: Has zebras, giraffes, elephants, penguins, and reptiles, in addition to a Children's Zoo, Tropical American Rain Forest, Wildlife Carousel, and Zoo Train.

see.name: Oxley Nature Center
see.desc: Hidden in the woods behind the Tulsa Zoo. Open almost all year. Has a few different habitats built up, such as a mini-prairie, a marsh with a walkover, ponds, woods, and plenty of opportunity for bird-watching.

see.name: Woodward Park
see.desc: See the park in the spring when the roses are blooming in the Tulsa Rose Garden.

see.name: Turkey Mountain
see.desc: Excellent location for hiking and mountain biking, with lots of side trails to explore. Features great views of Oral Roberts University and Downtown.

see.name: Blue Dome Arts Festival
see.desc: Running the same weekend as the critically acclaimed Mayfest. This festival showcases local Tulsa County area artists and lets them show their colors. Parking is limited, so be prepared to walk a few blocks. Middle of May.

see.name: Cherry Street Farmer's Market
see.desc: Every Saturday 'til the frost is on the pumpkin from about 7AM-11AM.

see.name: Mayfest
see.desc: If you're looking for that Unique Gift or piece of art you can't find elsewhere, You won't go away Empty-handed From here. with artists from all over the country, Mayfest is Truly the Cultural Highpoint of Tulsa's Yearly Calendar. (Middle of May, Same as Blue Dome Arts Festival)

see.name: Mini-Con
see.desc: Tulsa's Annual Anime Gathering is getting off the ground again after losing sponsors. Now sponsored by the Tulsa Library System, It is in good hands and could take a few years to get up to par with other conventions around the country. Has film-showings and merchandise sales (Date of Event Varies Year to Year).

see.name: Oklahoma Scottish Games & Gathering
see.desc: It's always the third weekend in September.

see.name: Tulsa Oktoberfest
see.desc: Which some people say is the largest Oktoberfest in the world outside of [[Germany]].

see.name: Tulsa State Fair
see.desc: At the Expo Fairgrounds (near 21st and Yale). It's the last full week in September. "Funnel cakes" are a tradition.

see.name: Wanenmacher's Tulsa Arms Show
see.desc: The world's largest gun show. Twice a year at the Expo Building. April and November.

eat.name: Albert G's
eat.desc: Tasty BBQ run out of an old gas station.

eat.name: Elmer's BBQ
eat.desc: This barbecue place is not to be missed, seeing Bill Clinton and other celebrities among its past patrons. "It be bad."

eat.name: Jamil's
eat.desc: Tulsa's oldest steakhouse. Known for Lebanese style appetizers (Tabouli, hummus, cabbage rolls, etc.) and desserts, along with traditional steakhouse fare.

eat.name: Rib Crib
eat.desc: Remarkably successful joint from midtown. Opened in 1992, but has managed to franchise into 8 states. The original location burned down a few years back, but they rebuilt this in its place.

eat.name: The Chalkboard
eat.desc: Fantastic bistro cuisine.

eat.name: Mahogany Prime Steakhouse
eat.desc: Some of the largest and best steaks. Very upscale and some of the best food in town. A great place to take an expense account.

eat.name: Palace Cafe
eat.desc: Fine dining restaurant featuring freshly prepared, local cuisine.

eat.name: Desi Wok
eat.desc: Serves traditional and fusion Indian/Chinese cuisine. Ask the large Filipino working behind the counter, William, for his "pineapple warrior" special. It's fantastic!

eat.name: India Palace
eat.desc: This little hole-in-the-wall is among Tulsa's best Indian restaurant. Try any of the dishes here, you can't go wrong.

eat.name: Zio's
eat.desc: Italian restaurant with very good pasta, family oriented.

eat.name: Sushi Train
eat.desc: Toy train delivers sushi.

eat.name: Sushi Hana
eat.desc: Expensive sushi.

eat.name: Yokozuna
eat.desc: Yokozuna is an Asian restaurant and sushi bar located in the historic Blue Dome District. Enjoy delicious food, unique drink selections, and relaxing atmosphere in Tulsa's great downtown.

eat.name: Gigi's
eat.desc: Renovated in 2020, it has a sushi bar. Has a good mix of authentic Cantonese cuisine and American favorites like lemon chicken.

eat.name: Casa Tequila Mexican Kitchen
eat.desc: Good for big groups, or solo trips. Menu is loaded with Mexican classics, and ranges from adult beverages to kid menus.

eat.name: Hideaway Pizza
eat.desc: Since 1957.

eat.name: Pie Hole Pizzeria
eat.desc: New York style slices at a good price. Amazing specialty pizzas.

eat.name: Savastano's
eat.desc: An "Authentic Chicago Style Pizzeria" that serves deep dish pizza. They stay true to Chicago style pizza by making that the theme of the entire restaurant. In the mood for a bar? Check out "The Friendly Confines" on the lower level of the restaurant. Accessible from the parking lot, this is the sports bar section of the restaurant open to anyone until night time when the bar closes to anyone under 21. The bar stays open later than its restaurant counterpart on the floor above.

eat.name: Tulsa's Incredible Pizza Company
eat.desc: It has {{sqft

eat.name: Umberto's Pizza
eat.desc: Has a "college" atmosphere--not upscale but friendly. Motto: "We toss ‘em, they're awesome."

eat.name: Andolini's
eat.desc: Considered the gourmet pizza chain in Tulsa, and thus a bit pricier, but the pizza is excellent.

eat.name: Saffron Mediterranean Cuisine
eat.desc: Thai buffet with lots of vegetarian options.

eat.name: Lanna Thai
eat.desc: Thai food with live band some nights.

eat.name: Elote Cafe & Catering
eat.desc: offers some vegan and vegetarian choices with luche libre or wrestling playing in the background.

eat.name: Arnie's Bar
eat.desc: Tulsa's Irish bar since 1956.

eat.name: The Max Retropub
eat.desc: Late 1980s-early 1990s themed bar and arcade, featuring Skeeball and tons of arcade cabinets many Gen X'ers will remember from their childhood. Also featuring gourmet junkfood.

eat.name: Kilkenny's Irish Pub
eat.desc: Has a nice selection of beers, nice atmosphere and good food. Pours the best Guinness. A little more upscale than McNellie's.

eat.name: McNellie's Public House
eat.desc: An Irish pub with over 60 beers on tap.

eat.name: White Lion Pub
eat.desc: A very authentic pub in South Tulsa. The proprietor brought much of the furniture and decor from an actual pub in England. They serve English food and drink. Make sure to try the "Brown Bitter" ale.

eat.name: DoubleShot Coffee Company
eat.desc: Local coffee roaster and barista, DoubleShot caters to Tulsa's coffee snobs and neighbourhood residents. Be sure to ask the staff about their trips to origin.

eat.name: Gypsy Coffee House & Cyber Cafe
eat.desc: Tulsa only late night coffee house downtown, great desserts and the best espresso. Good deli-style food. Free wi-fi.

eat.name: Shades of Brown
eat.desc: Offers quality coffee in a friendly environment. They feature local art on display, with a different artist every month. They also have live music in the evenings.

eat.name: Mercury Lounge
eat.desc: Rockabilly music with a $5 beer and shot special.

see.name: High Desert Museum
see.desc: The High Desert Museum is just south of Bend on Highway 97. The High Desert Museum is a great way to gain educational experience about some of the animals and habitat that go along with Central Oregon.

see.name: Pilot Butte State Scenic Viewpoint
see.desc: A 500-foot-tall cinder cone in the center of Bend that offers an excellent view of the city and surroundings. Pilot Butte makes Bend one of the few cities in the U.S. to have a volcano within its boundaries. Drive or hike to the top.

see.name: Newberry National Volcanic Monument
see.desc: See lava flows, explore lava caves and ice caves, fishing for trophy rainbow and brown trout in the two alpine lakes at the Newberry caldera (East Lake & Paulina Lake) and explore the massive Obsidian Flow, where very little has been able to grow for several thousand years. There are hiking trails, camping and resorts. Also snow parks, winter cross-country skiing and snowmobiling. Visit the Lava Lands Visitor Center for information.

see.name: Smith Rock
see.desc: Smith Rock State Park encompasses 651 acres on the Oregon high desert plateau which hovers around 3000 feet in elevation. The park and campground are open year-round. A $5 day use permit or a current state park camp receipt is needed for each vehicle. A yearly permit is available for $30. Hiking trails offer spectacular views of the surrounding area. You can spend 30 minutes walking along the river or a half day making a loop on the entire trail system that extends outside of the park. The major rock faces are composed of welded tuff (compressed volcanic ash) reaching a height of up to 550 feet. The picnic and campground areas sit on top of the rimrock which is made up of columnar basalt. There are over 1400 climbing routes in and around the park ranging from some of the best sport climbs in the world to. “Why would anyone want to climb that pile of choss”. People climb year-round, but summer temperatures can reach over {{F

see.name: Deschutes River
see.desc: The Deschutes features ruggedly beautiful scenery, outstanding whitewater boating, and a renowned sport fishery for steelhead, brown trout, and native rainbow trout. The Upper Deschutes features primarily flatwater boating with limited whitewater and excellent trout fishing opportunities. The Middle Deschutes has excellent hiking opportunities with spectacular geologic formations and waterfalls, but boating is limited. The Lower Deschutes offers the greatest opportunities for whitewater rafting and is one of Oregon's premier steelhead and trout fisheries

see.name: Cascade lakes and Mountains
see.desc: These areas are spectacular. Take a drive on the Cascade Lakes Highway and you can go to Sparks Lake, which is ideal for canoeing and kayaking, the Twin Lakes, Elk Lake and more while taking in some beautiful mountain scenery at the same time. Many of these lakes offer fishing, camping, and trailheads for hiking up into the mountains. Along the Cascade Lakes Highway, you can access trailheads as well as snow parks for snowmobiling in the winter.

see.name: Cultus Lake
see.desc: About 45 minutes outside of Bend, Oregon, on the cascades lake highway. At the lake there are a number of activities and facilities available for tourists, all centered around the crystal clear waters of the lake. At Cultus Lake there are a number of activities available. The resort's main attraction is its water sports. One can rent a number of watercrafts including jet skis, motorboats, canoes, kayaks, paddleboats and party boats. Gas and oil can be purchased on site. Another popular activity at Cultus is the fishing. The lake is filled with Rainbows, Bass, Mackinaws and Browns. There are also beaches where people can swim and enjoy the water from another perspective. At the lodge there is a restaurant open to the public. They serve a wide variety of food here and it is reasonably priced. One can also purchase groceries, although the selection is limited and prices higher than a supermarket. Cabins are available to rent at Cultus Lake. The cabins are near the lake, and have fireplaces, kitchens and appliances. There are a number of campsites available on and near the lake. They are operated by the National Forest Service, and have a small per night fee. There is running water, toilets and parking available to campers, however there are no RV hook ups.

see.name: Elk Lake
see.desc: About 11 miles past Mount Bachelor and just a short drive out of Bend. It is known for its mountain scenery and relaxed atmosphere. It has clear water, making it popular to people seeking water activities. The Lake is 405 acres in size, with a depths ranging from 25-75 ft. The elevation of the resort is about 4884 ft. At Elk Lake, fishing is a popular activity. The lake is filled with Kokanee and brook trout. In the summer months the lake is planted with brook trout. Popular fishing techniques include: still-fishing, trolling and fly fishing. Boating is also permitted at Elk Lake. At the resort there are paddle boat, canoes, and sail boats available to rent. Prices for these boats are fairly reasonable and can be checked out by the hour or by the day. Larger motor boats are not allowed to help maintain the peacefulness on the lake. There are a number of boat docks that surround the lake to make launching a boat relatively easy. Swimming is easily accessible at the sunset and beach areas of the lake. If hiking is your choice there are miles of trails that circle the lake. At the resort there is a restaurant open to the public. It serves a wide variety of food, specializing in their hamburgers. For dessert they have a small ice cream parlor with about a dozen different flavors. There is also a small store where groceries can be purchased. Cabins are available to rent, and can be checked out at the main resort. They vary in size and location. Camping can be done at a number of different sites in the area. The different sites include: Little Fawn Campground, Little Fawn Group Camp, Point Campground, and Elk Lake Campground. There are also areas reserved specifically for day use.

see.name: Mt. Bachelor
see.desc: Bachelor is Central Oregon's best Ski/Snowboard mountain. It was home to the Olympic snowboard trials years back as well. When the summit is open (depending on weather) it is some of the best skiing you will find in Oregon with 360-degree access to the entire mountain. The northwest territory is also great with lots of black diamond runs. It's probably not a bad idea to take some 2-way radios for the other members of your party. The mountain is quite big and keeping track of everyone is sometimes difficult.

see.name: Pine Mountain Observatory
see.desc: Great place to go see the stars. Camping available onsite. Check the website to see when the observatory is open or if events are occurring.

see.name: Hayden Homes Amphitheater
see.desc: In the summer time Bend offers many Sunday concerts that are performed at the Les Schwab Amphitheater. In the past artists such as Cold Play, Keith Urban, Lynyrd Skynyrd, ZZ Top and Jack Johnson have performed there. Buy tickets at The Ticket Mill store in the Old Mill District, or online. The Amphitheater also hosts the Bend Brewfest each May, with many local and West Coast beers, ciders, and seltzers.

see.name: High Desert River Outfitters
see.desc: Specializes in Oregon river rafting and Oregon whitewater rafting.

see.name: Smith Rock Climbing School
see.desc: AMGA Accredited guide service. Guiding and instructing at Smith Rock since 1983. Smith Rock's original guide service.

see.name: Big Mountain Heli Tours
see.desc: Bend scenic helicopter tours, trips and charters. Discover wine tasting helicopter tours, scenic helicopter tours at the Cascade range, outdoor tours and activities year round.

see.name: Timberline Mountain Guides
see.desc: Backcountry skiing and snowboarding. Instruction, tours, ski mountaineering. AMGA accredited guide service.

eat.name: Longboard Louie's
eat.desc: A great burrito shack on the east side of Bend that offers great food at prices college kids can afford. Louie's has all of the character of the locals and it is a couple hundred yards the base of Pilot Butte.

eat.name: Miyagi Ramen
eat.desc: Great ramen shop centrally located in Bend.

eat.name: The Sparrow Bakery Northwest
eat.desc: The Sparrow Bakery Northwest is the second of their restaurants in Bend. In addition to Ocean Rolls and breakfast sandwiches, they offer a variety of foods for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

eat.name: Deschutes Brewery Public House
eat.desc: Notable for its world-renowned dark brews, the Deschutes Brewery Public House offers excellent burgers and sandwiches with a laid-back atmosphere in the heart of downtown Bend. (You can also visit the brewery and get a tour of the beer production facilities).

eat.name: Wild Rose Northern Thai Eats
eat.desc: Excellent Northern Thai eatery. Being northern style Thai, their specialties are fried chicken wings and stir fries rather than curries and pad thai that you might get at a typical Thai restaurant.

eat.name: Pine Tavern Restaurant & Bar
eat.desc: Founded in 1936, serves classic American entrées made with fresh local ingredients.

eat.name: Anthony's
eat.desc: A Pacific Northwest regional chain that offers excellent seafood. It has a nice full service bar with about six of the Oregon microbrews on tap. It also has a nice patio area that overlooks the Deschutes River

eat.name: Zydeco Kitchen & Cocktails
eat.desc: Try the Acadian Flatbread from the starter list. Good wine list and full service bar.

eat.name: Bontà Natural Artisan Gelato
eat.desc: A wide array of gelato scoops make this a sought-after stop on a hot afternoon.

eat.name: Goody's Chocolates and Ice Cream
eat.desc: Goody's is a delightful little candy shop in downtown Bend that offers an array of different sorts of chocolates, candies, milkshakes, ice creams, and popcorn that is perfect for topping off a great meal.

eat.name: Astro Lounge
eat.desc: Singles bar in downtown area. This is a late night hot spot in Bend.

eat.name: El Rodeo
eat.desc: Friendly staff, family friendly, consistently fast meal preparation & a local favorite.

eat.name: Deschutes Brewery Tasting Room
eat.desc: Some great seasonal brews as well as six others that are regularly on tap. The facility is in the heart of downtown Bend, which is next to the Deschutes River. Deschutes Brewery's "Mirror Pond Pale Ale" was once voted the number one microbrew in the United States by Men's Journal. Other Deschutes offerings have also won national and international awards. Free daily tours of the brewery at offered at the top of the hour from 1-4PM. Online reservations are encouraged for tours, but walk-ins are allowed if there's room. Known to local college students the brewery burger and a beer sampler gets you fed and watered in style for cheap.

eat.name: Bend Brewing Company
eat.desc: The Bend Brewing Company is another great place to grab a drink right in downtown Bend. BBC has also won several awards for their beers. The riverside pub and restaurant overlooks Mirror Pond.

eat.name: Worthy Brewing
eat.desc: Huge brewery serves burgers and pizza with lots of indoor or outdoor seating. The observatory ("Hopservatory") on the roof is open after 9PM on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights.

eat.name: Boneyard Beer Pub
eat.desc: Serving flights of beer and Latin/Asian fusion dishes.

eat.name: 10 Barrel Brewing
eat.desc: Serves pizza and burgers alongside flights of beer.

eat.name: Silver Moon Brewing
eat.desc: Great beer and good service. Free Wifi. 10 craft beers available. The Hounds Tooth Amber is one of the best around.

see.name: University of Oregon
see.desc: Essentially the center of the town, and the reason for the town's modern growth.

see.name: Oregon Ducks
see.desc: The teams representing the University of Oregon, competing in the Big Ten Conference following the 2024 collapse of the Pac-12 Conference, are Eugene's most famous contribution to the sports world. Ducks sports have benefited enormously from the financial support of Phil Knight, UO alum and now-retired head of Oregon-based sports equipment giant Nike. The highest-profile Oregon team is the football team, which rose to become a perennial national contender in the early 2000s and also infamous for its highly colorful and variable uniforms. Oregon also has an extremely rich tradition in track and field, with Hayward Field known for its enthusiastic fans; the city has become known as "Track Town USA" because of this. Hayward Field was rebuilt in a project that was completed in 2021; the new stadium, expandable to 30,000, hosted the 2022 World Athletics Championships. The main sporting venues (including Hayward Field) are all on campus. The football stadium, Autzen Stadium, is famous as one of the loudest and most intimidating venues in American sports. The basketball teams have played at Matthew Knight Arena (nicknamed "Matt Arena"; named for Phil's son, who died in a scuba diving accident) since 2011. Ducks baseball plays at PK Park (not named for Knight), which is shared with the minor-league professional Eugene Emeralds.

see.name: Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art
see.desc: At the University of Oregon. Free on Wednesdays between 5PM and 8PM.

see.name: Museum of Natural and Cultural History
see.desc: At the University of Oregon.

see.name: Pioneer Statue
see.desc: Many claim "The Simpsons" statue of Jebediah Springfield is based on the bronze pioneer statue on the University of Oregon campus. Installed in 1919 by Alexander Phimister Proctor, it depicts a trapper carrying a rifle.

see.name: Eugene Emeralds Baseball
see.desc: Minor League Baseball team with games during the summer.

see.name: Hayward Field
see.desc: One of the best-known historic track and field stadiums in the United States. Hayward Field has hosted three Olympic Trials, and a variety of National, NCAA, and Masters championships. University of Oregon. It hosted the 2022 World Athletics Championships.

see.name: Pre's Rock
see.desc: A memorial to Olympic runner and local legend, Steve Prefontaine, at the site of his fatal car crash. The Prefontaine Classic, is held annually in Eugene in his honor.

see.name: Maude Kerns Art Center
see.desc: A non-profit art gallery housed in a historic church building built in 1895. Known for its annual [[Day of the Dead]] (Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead)]] exhibit in October.

see.name: Cascades Raptor Center
see.desc: The Cascades Raptor Center is a nature center and wildlife hospital that specializes in raptor rehabilitation.

see.name: Wayne Morse Family Farm
see.desc: The Wayne Morse Family Farm, a City of Eugene park, was the home of Oregon's long-time United States Senator, Wayne Morse. The 27-acre (110,000 m²) home used to be a working farm called Edgewood Farm. Owned by the Morse family, it includes the Morse home, a natural wooded area, and an open meadow. Formerly named Morse Ranch, the park is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

see.name: Oregon Wine Tours
see.desc: Sunshine Limo Service and Wine Tours: Local tour operator, specializing in Willamette Valley wine tours. A safe way to enjoy wine tasting in comfort and style.

see.name: John G. Shedd Institute for the Arts
New Zone Gallery
see.desc: The New Zone Gallery, a non-profit cooperative gallery, features an eclectic mix of styles, techniques and media, created by its 70 artist members. Monthly/bi-monthly changing shows. It has a gift shop.

see.name: Oregon Contemporary Theatre
see.desc: Formerly the Lord Leebrick Theatre Company. Community theater with a diverse schedule. See website for current shows and times.

see.name: Actors Cabaret of Eugene
see.desc: Local dinner theater in downtown. See website for current shows and times.

see.name: Bijou Arts Cinema
see.desc: A unique, two-screen arts cinema housed in a cool old church/mortuary. Shows indie movies. A second location, the Bijou Metro, has opened downtown on Broadway.

see.name: Cuthbert Amphitheater
see.desc: An outdoor music venue in Alton Baker Park that gets some pretty big shows. Since it's outdoors, you can hear just fine throughout the park. During most shows, the real party is in the park in front of and around the amphitheater.

see.name: Hult Center for the Performing Arts
see.desc: Large performing arts center.

see.name: WOW Hall
see.desc: Small concert hall featuring alternative performances. Ask about work trade opportunities between 3PM and 6PM Monday through Friday--maybe you'll get to see the show for free!

see.name: Spencer Butte
see.desc: A large hill south of downtown. Head south on Willamette St about {{mi

see.name: Skinner Butte Park
see.desc: Skinner Butte is just north of downtown, and offers hiking paths that lead to the summit (though you can also drive to the top in a car) where a tree-free view of the city and surrounding mountains can be seen. The area of the park between the butte and the Willamette River has more traditional park amenities like a playground and meeting space. If the weather is nice, people will often climb the exposed basalt cliffs on the west side of the butte (with the proper training and gear, of course!) The butte was the original site of city founder Eugene Skinner's cabin and the park is named in his honor.

see.name: Ridgeline trail
see.desc: Extensive set of hiking trails south of town. To find them, head south on Willamette St., {{mi

see.name: Amazon Trail
see.desc: {{mi

see.name: Rexius Trail
see.desc: {{mi

see.name: Pre's Trail
see.desc: {{mi

see.name: Ruth Bascom Riverbank Path System
see.desc: Eugene has more pedestrian bridges across the Willamette River than those that allow auto traffic, and all of them can be accessed via the Bascom path system. Renting a bicycle (see Get Around) and riding along the river is an excellent way to spend a pleasant afternoon and tour the city's waterfront.

see.name: Disc golf
see.desc: There is an 18-hole course in Alton Baker Park and a smaller, (often crowded) 9-hole course at Westmoreland Park in West Eugene.

see.name: Skate
see.desc: There are many skate parks throughout the city.

see.name: WJ Skatepark + Urban Plaza
see.desc: The largest covered skate park in the country.

see.name: ASUO Street Fair
see.desc: Bi-annual student street fair kind of like Saturday market, but more student-oriented. Fall/Spring terms.

see.name: Sasquatch Brewfest
see.desc: Craft beer festival with live music (early June).

see.name: Oregon Bach Festival
see.desc: Held late June through mid-July; presented by the University of Oregon.

see.name: Oregon Country Fair
see.desc: Second weekend in July. One of the biggest "hippie" gatherings, held in nearby Veneta. Tons of great food, great hand made products sold by local vendors, and live music to be had.

see.name: Lane County Fair
see.desc: An annual mid-summer celebration featuring food, music and other entertainment.

see.name: Whiteaker Block Party
see.desc: August. Large, free outdoor festival in the Whiteaker neighborhood: Live music, street performances, food, drink, etc.

see.name: Scandinavian Festival
see.desc: An annual Scandinavian-themed festival in nearby Junction City that has been happening for more than 50 years. August.

see.name: Mushroom Festival
see.desc: Mushroom-themed harvest festival. October.

see.name: Clayfest
see.desc: October. A three-day ceramics only show and sale featuring over 60 local artists. Clay Fest draws artists from all over Oregon. This is a great opportunity buy unique handmade pieces directly from the artists who make the work.

eat.name: Mezza Luna Pizzeria
eat.desc: Serves lunch and dinner, real NY style pizza, with a variety of meat and vegetarian choices, plus the option to create your own pizza from a large list of toppings.

eat.name: Off The Waffle
eat.desc: Serving authentic Liege waffles with an amazing assortment of toppings, such as bacon, cardamom, garlic, fruit, and the list goes on and on. Also serves omelettes and they have some local microbrew on tap.

eat.name: SeQuential
eat.desc: Serving fresh made sandwiches, coffee, bakery items, sweets, snacks and beer. Mini health food market and cafe with drive-through window for coffee. Omnivorous, herbivorous and diets of all kinds.

eat.name: El Super Burrito
eat.desc: Very inexpensive and locally owned. El Super Burrito is the best burrito and taco you can get for your money in the city.

eat.name: Voodoo Doughnut Tres
eat.desc: A fun-but-gimmicky doughnut store chain with additional locations in Denver and Portland. Known for unusual toppings like bacon slices with maple-frosting, Capn' Crunch, and powdered Tang.

eat.name: El Super Taco
eat.desc: Great Mexican food on a budget.

eat.name: Brail's
eat.desc: Two locations where you can get a hearty traditional American breakfast at a reasonable price. Expect a wait for weekend brunch.

eat.name: Morning Glory
eat.desc: Breakfast.

eat.name: Sweet Life
eat.desc: World-class desserts, including vegan options. Very popular among both locals and visitors, so expect a long line on weekend evenings.

eat.name: Chacha’s Hawaiian Grill
eat.desc: Pretty good Hawaiian food in a very relaxed environment.

eat.name: Sushi Seoul
eat.desc: A cool sushi place downtown. A cool interior with happy hour.

eat.name: Rye
eat.desc: Reservations recommended for dinner. A restaurant with a speakeasy veneer serving a globally-inspired menu that uses fresh, local ingredients.

eat.name: The Cafe Med
eat.desc: A small, upscale Italian restaurant where you can try some mussels or bolognese and a tiramisu afterwards.

eat.name: Mazzi's
eat.desc: Has the best Italian food in town. Prices are reasonable, considering the quality of the food; a typical dish is $12-18. Outstanding wine selection as well.

eat.name: The Bier Stein Bottleshop and Pub
eat.desc: Eugene's largest beer selection, more than 1,000 bottled beers and ten beers on draft.

eat.name: Luckey's Club Cigar Store
eat.desc: Eugene's oldest bar and one of the oldest pool halls on the West Coast. They still have a few tables, but have transformed into one of Eugene's leading music venues with several shows a week.

eat.name: Max's Tavern
eat.desc: Popular little student bar, rumored to be the inspiration for Moe's Tavern in The Simpsons. Happy hour daily from 4PM to 8PM. They have darts and an outdoor patio.

eat.name: Blairally Vintage Arcade
eat.desc: Combination bar/pinball arcade in Whiteaker. Great collection of pinball machines, 1980s arcade games and beer. Darkstalkers appears to be a particular favorite. Most Blazers games shown here.

eat.name: Sam Bond's Garage
eat.desc: Funky neighborhood bar and music venue. Live music on weekends.

eat.name: Ninkasi Brewing Company
eat.desc: A production brewery of high quality beers, ales and lagers since 2006, tasting room and patio with firepits and heat lamps.

eat.name: Oakshire Brewing
eat.desc: A Eugene craft brewery known for its Watershed IPA and Overcast Espresso Stout.

eat.name: Falling Sky Brewing House
eat.desc: A Northwest brewery & gastro-pub inspired by the convivial atmosphere of Munich beer halls.

eat.name: High Street Brewery & Cafe
eat.desc: A McMenamins pub with McMenamins beers as well as national and local micro brews.

eat.name: North Bank
eat.desc: A McMenamins pub with McMenamins beers. Every table has a Willamette River view. Has a tiki-themed Kapu Hut.

eat.name: Viking Braggot Company
eat.desc: Produces braggots traditional ale/mead fusion.

eat.name: Espresso Roma
eat.desc: Popular coffee shop a block from campus. Good coffee, nice patio.

eat.name: Iris Vineyard
eat.desc: ''Temporarily closed as of 2022; call ahead''. Specializes in producing small quantities of quality, hand-crafted Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, and Chardonnay. Iris Hill has been dedicated to growing high quality fruit through sustainable viticultural practices.

eat.name: King Estate
eat.desc: The {{acre

see.name: Portland World Naked Bike Ride
see.desc: Portland's annual World Naked Bike Ride, held in early June, has many goals: to increase visibility of cyclists; to promote confidence in the beauty and individuality of the human body; to affirm nudity as a legal form of protest; to emphasize the bicycles’s place as a catalyst for change in the future of sustainability, transport, community and recreation; to celebrate the coming summer, bicycles in the urban grid, and the fun of a multi-thousand person bike ride; and to protest the automobile. World Naked Bike Ride is an annual, worldwide bike ride that highlights the vulnerability of cyclists everywhere and decries society’s dependence on pollution-based transport.

see.name: Portland Rose Festival
see.desc: Portland's annual Rose Festival is held every year at the beginning of June. The largest event of the year includes multiple parades, a carnival at waterfront park, and several military ships docked for fleet week.

see.name: Portland Thorns FC
see.desc: The Portland Thorns are the local women's' soccer team who play in the NWSL. They are known to draw a consistently sizeable crowd of fans and have performed well in league play since the founding of the club in 2013, winning three championships since.

see.name: Portland Timbers FC
see.desc: The Portland Timbers are Portland's Major League Soccer team. Their most ardent supporters are known as the Timbers Army who sit at the north end of the stadium singing and chanting through the entire match. Visitors are both encouraged and welcomed to join by buying a general admission ticket and lining up hours before the game to get the best seats (if you so choose). If you'd prefer to watch the game and enjoy the energy of the Army from a distance (perhaps if traveling with young children), seating in assigned areas is also available.

see.name: Portland Trail Blazers
see.desc: The Portland Trail Blazers play in NBA. The Moda Center is centrally located near downtown next to four MAX lines for those who are interested in catching a game. Nearly every game is a full house, and there aren't many NBA venues that have the same energy for the same value as a Blazer game.

eat.name: Cha! Cha! Cha!
eat.desc: 'Rritos, 'ritas, and more. Good quality Mexican food at a middling price. Focus on local, sustainable, and healthy.

eat.name: New Seasons Market
eat.desc: Local natural food supermarket chain with fantastic sandwiches and an awesome deli counter. You can choose your bread, meat/tofu pate, veggies, and spreads. Six locations in the city.

eat.name: Nicholas Restaurant
eat.desc: Great value Lebanese food, family owned and operated where everything is made from scratch. Two locations.

eat.name: ¿Por Qué No?
eat.desc: Popular taqueria providing sophisticated but informal food in an evocative setting. Top-notch tortillas that are often purchased on their own. Excellent array of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, including authentic drinks not often seen north of the border (horchata, mezcal, ''etc.''). Often crowded with lines, especially at mealtimes, but quick service keeps you from waiting too long. Outdoor seating. Kid and bike friendly. Order ahead for take-out and skip the line.

eat.name: Sizzle Pie
eat.desc: A heavy metal-themed pizza joint with some of the best pies in town. Pizza is available by the slice or whole, to eat there or to go. The salads are great as well utilizing yummy homemade dressings. Great for vegans, vegetarians, and omnivores alike! Two locations in Portland.

eat.name: Taqueria Los Gorditos
eat.desc: Vegan and non-vegan food, cheap but delicious and with a very expansive menu for a taco cart (they also have three brick-and-mortar locations), including quite large burritos. The ingredients are fresh and the staff friendly.
